#849. Vote for the first BBC Men's Footballer of the Year

Voting is now open for the BBC Men's Footballer of the Year 2026 award, which will be presented at Sports Personality of the Year.

Fans from the UK can vote from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal.

The vote closes on Friday, 27 November at 09:00 GMT.

The winner of the award - new for this year - will be presented during the live Sports Personality of the Year show on Sunday, 13 December.

Alex Kay-Jelski, Director of BBC Sport, said: "From the drama and excitement of the men's World Cup to the moments that have captivated fans across the domestic and international game, 2026 has given us so much to celebrate.

"Our inaugural BBC Men's Footballer of the Year award is about recognising the players who have made this year so special, inspired fans and left their mark on the game.

"It's a fantastic shortlist, and I can't wait to see who the public choose as our first-ever winner."

The shortlist was selected by an expert panel comprising former international players and some of the BBC's most respected football voices, bringing together a wealth of experience and insight from across the game.

The panel included Cesar Azpilicueta (Spain), Scott Brown (Scotland), Olivier Giroud (France), Shay Given (Republic of Ireland), Hassan Kachloul (Morocco), Lucas Leiva (Brazil), Benni McCarthy (South Africa), Alan Shearer, Ellen White (both England) and Ashley Williams (Wales).

Read more on the five contenders and cast your vote below.

Sorry, this vote cannot be loaded. In order to vote you need to enable JavaScript in your browser.

Meet the SPOTY Men's Footballer of the Year contenders

Bellingham made history this summer as he became the first Englishman to score as many as seven goals at a major tournament.

In a superb World Cup for the midfielder, he memorably netted twice in back-to-back games to help the Three Lions beat Mexico and Norway.

That meant he joined exalted company as the first player to score two or more goals in successive World Cup knockout games since Diego Maradona in 1986, and the second youngest in history behind Pele in 1958.

Bellingham also became the youngest European player to make an appearance at four different major tournaments, and also reached the milestone of 50 caps at a younger age than any other England men's player.

The goals continued to flow for Real Madrid, too, with Bellingham notching his 50th for the club to move above the legendary Zinedine Zidane in the Los Blancos' all-time scoring charts.

Bellingham was recently joined in the England squad by his brother Jobe

In a stunning year of goalscoring, Kane become the first Englishman for 25 years (and only fifth in history) to win the Ballon d'Or - awarded to the world's best footballer.

His tally of 73 goals in 65 matches for club and country during a stellar 2025-26 season has only been surpassed in one of Europe's top five leagues by Lionel Messi's 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12.

Kane scored 61 of those goals in just 51 appearances for Bayern Munich as he helped the Bavarians to a league and cup double. His total was 19 more than any other player in Europe's top five divisions.

Already England's record goalscorer, he surpassed Peter Shilton's mark of 125 appearances to become the most-capped Englishman in history.

Six goals at this summer's World Cup also helped him overtake Gary Lineker as the Three Lions' record scorer at the tournament, while he joined David Beckham as the only Englishmen to score in three separate World Cups.

Kane scored his first England goal 79 seconds into his debut in 2015

Mbappe came out on top of an enthralling tussle with Lionel Messi at the 2026 World Cup to become the leading goalscorer in the tournament's history.

The France forward, who is still only 27, took his tally to 22 from just three World Cups to finish one ahead of the great Argentine.

Mbappe's 10 goals from eight games this summer meant he won his second World Cup Golden Boot - a feat no player has managed before.

It also made him the first man to reach double figures at a World Cup since Gerd Muller in 1970, with only Just Fontaine (13) and Sandor Kocsis (11) having scored more goals in a single tournament.

Other achievements in a standout year included him finishing runner-up in the Ballon d'Or awards and overtaking Olivier Giroud as France's all-time leading goalscorer.

He scored 25 times to retain his title as La Liga's top scorer during a 2025-26 campaign in which he netted 42 goals in all competitions for Real Madrid.

Mbappe has won eight consecutive league golden boots

Midfield maestro Rodri earned yet another accolade in his incredible career when he was awarded the Golden Ball trophy for the World Cup's best player.

By captaining Spain to glory in the US, Rodri became only the fourth male player to win the World Cup, European Championship, Champions League and Ballon d'Or - following in the footsteps of legendary Germans Gerd Muller and Franz Beckenbauer and France's Zinedine Zidane.

His achievements were made all the more special given doubts remained over whether he would recapture his best form after a long recovery from a serious knee injury in 2024.

Then Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola predicted he would return to his best at the World Cup and he was right. Rodri completed 756 passes there - the most in the tournament since records began in 1966.

His final season at Manchester City before departing for Barcelona ended in familiar fashion with a domestic cup double taking his trophy haul with the club to 14.

Rodri scored the goal that won Manchester City the Champions League in 2023

Lamine Yamal continues to rewrite the record books with his astonishing exploits for club and country.

Just days after his 19th birthday, the Spaniard became the youngest footballer to have played in - and won - both a World Cup and a European Championship. The only players younger than him to play in a World Cup final are Brazil's Pele in 1958 and Giuseppe Bergomi for Italy in 1982.

For the second year running, his performances led to a podium place at the Ballon d'Or and at the same award ceremony he became the first footballer in history to win the Young Talent of the Year three years in succession.

At club level, he was named La Liga's Best Player courtesy of a starring role in Barcelona's title success. The teenager ended the season with an impressive 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions.

He recently broke Kylian Mbappe's record for the most goals by a teenager in Champions League history.

Lamine Yamal was 16 years and 362 days when he scored at the European Championship in 2024

#848. Are Pete Davidson and Sarah Jane Nader Officially Dating? The Truth

Amid speculation that Pete Davidson is dating Love Thy Nader star Sarah Jane Nader, a source close to the Saturday Night Live star told E! News the truth about the pair.

Pete Davidson isn’t adding a new romance to his Saturday night.

Amid speculation that the Saturday Night Live alum has started a new relationship with Sarah Jane Nader, a source close to Davidson told E! News there is no truth to the rumors.

According to the source, the two are just friends, adding that they have only seen each other a handful of times since they were first spotted together at the beginning of August.

At the time, Davidson, 33, and Nader, 24, stepped out in Brooklyn and got into a car together with the comedian opening the passenger door for the Love Thy Nader star before moving to the driver’s side. Still, a source with direct knowledge also told E! News in August that the pair are just friends.

And rumors about the duo also came as a surprise to Nader’s sister Brooks Nader.

“Oh wow, I thought she was into girls this week,” she joked to TMZ shortly after the pair’s outing. “That’s what her vibe has been.”

The Baywatch star added that she hadn’t spoken to her sister about the speculation, adding, “I really did think that she was into girls recently, but she keeps us on our toes.”

As for Davidson, the How to Rob a Bank star has kept a low profile with his love life since he and ex Elsie Hewitt split earlier this year, months after they welcomed daughter Scottie Rose, 11 months.

And becoming a dad has also led to a personal transformation for Davidson, especially when it came to how he looked at his career.

"My priorities have shifted in just that becoming a dad is great for so many reasons," he told E! News in September, "but it just made me realize the stuff that I cared about so much don't actually matter.”

In fact, the most important person in his life at the moment is his baby girl.

"Now the priority is if I don't get that whatever job or whatever, who cares?" Davidson continued. "I get to be home with Scottie. That's awesome."

Welcoming his daughter has not only changed his outlook on his career, but has also had a profound effect on his general disposition.

"It's calmed [me] down," he added. "My eagerness to like—I don't know—be out there very much. I'm just happy where I am."

For a deep dive into Davidson’s fascinating dating history, keep reading.

Davidson briefly dated the Girl Code star in 2015—and he remains close friends with the fellow comedian. They were spotted hanging out after one of his comedy shows in February 2019 and Aquilino co-starred in his 2020 film, The King of Staten Island.

David, the daughter of Curb Your Enthusiasm's Larry David, revealed a lot about her two-and-a-half year romance with Davidson in her 2020 book of essays, No One Asked For This. The couple first began dating in 2016, with David writing that they were "kindred spirits." But she admitted Davidson's mental health struggles had taken a toll on her.

"Previously, self-harm and suicide threats had come about from trivial circumstances, incidents that would go from 0 to 100, which were so momentarily urgent, like the last minute of an escape room before the time goes off, except I'm the only one in the room and all the clues are tricks," she recalled. "Once he was back in a good headspace, I wouldn't be able to bring myself to do it either; I was too mentally exhausted to do anything besides emotionally recover from the chaos of the week before."

After she ended their relationship while on a family trip in 2018, David attempted to reconcile with Davidson in a moment of weakness. But she was shocked when he later sent her a text message to reveal he had moved on.

Two days later, she opened Instagram to see her ex had "uploaded a photo of himself with his hand covering his face to show off his new finger tattoos," she wrote. "My name, which had been written in cursive across his ring finger, was now covered over with black ink."

Weeks after Davidson and David's breakup—and not long after Grande's split from rapper Mac Miller—E! News confirmed that the actor and the pop star were casually dating.

But things went from casual to serious AF when the couple—who met when she hosted SNL two years earlier—went Instagram official and got matching tattoos by their one-month anniversary. And by June of 2018, the pair were engaged and living together in a $16 million NYC loft alongside their adopted pet pig.

Their whirlwind romance came to an end in October 2018, with the news of the split coming one month after Miller was found dead of an overdose at age 26.

Davidson processed the breakup by using it in his standup comedy sets, while Grande channeled her feelings into a hit song and album, thank u, next.

Three months after his split from Grande, the King of Staten Island star kicked off a breezy romance with Beckinsale.

"They spend most of their time on opposite coasts so it's a casual thing," a source told E! News at the time. "But they are going to keep talking and having fun together."

During the course of their brief courtship, Davidson and the Underworld star attended parties, hockey games and even enjoyed dinner with Beckinsale's parents. But the romance fizzled out after three months, a source explaining that it had simply "ran its course," adding, "They still talk and are very friendly."

The comedian and the Once Upon a Time in Hollywood star first sparked dating rumors in August 2019 when they were seen together in Venice for the premiere of Qualley's film, Seberg. The two were then spotted on a romantic stroll, walking hand-in-hand as they explored the city.

While neither Davidson nor Qualley ever confirmed their romance, her mom Andie MacDowell ended up spilling the beans in an interview. "She has a beautiful relationship with him but I don't want to step on her relationship too much," MacDowell told People. "They have a nice relationship."

But the couple called it quits after two months.

Davidson and Gerber—the daughter of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber—began dating in October 2019, quickly becoming inseparable as they were spotted out and about in NYC.

But weeks into their romance, the then-18-year-old's concerned parents intervened, a source telling E! News that they were trying to "guide [Kaia] and to help Pete through a difficult time."

By January 2020, another insider close to Davidson told E! his relationship with Gerber was "cooling off" as he prioritized his mental health by seeking treatment. A third source said "there was no bad blood" between the pair.

Let's hope Lady Whistledown wasn't upset she was scooped by the paparazzi when Davidson was spotted with the Bridgerton breakout star in April 2021. The two were snapped in England getting cozy outside of a grocery store and appeared to take a playful stroll together in a field.

Throughout their months-long romance, the couple offered several clues about their coupling. They were spotted wearing matching silver monogrammed necklaces bearing their shared initials, "PD," and Davidson said the actress was his "celebrity crush" in a Zoom Q&A with college students.

"It just goes back to being naïve—I didn't think anyone would care," she later told Elle of their experience. "I was just being a young woman and dating and somehow that provokes a conversation. There were lots of hard lessons I had to learn through basically just having a personal life."

A source close to Davidson told E! News that he was "very into Phoebe" and had been flying back and forth from NYC to the U.K. The insider explained, "He doesn't mind, because he's very excited about spending time with her."

However, by August, they had split. "The long distance made it very difficult," a source shared with E! News. "They had fun, but it wasn't sustainable being so far apart. It was great while it lasted, but they both agreed it was best to move on."

For nearly a year, Davidson and The Kardashians star enjoyed quite the ride, going public with their romance during an October 2021 outing at Knott's Scary Farm just weeks after her SNL hosting gig. And while the mother of four showed the Aladdin to her Jasmine a whole new world—he joined her on a trip to Tahiti, on her family's Hulu reality series and even on the Met Gala red carpet—by August 2022, the two had come back down to earth. Despite maintaining "a lot of love and respect for each other," a source told E! News, NYC-based Davidson and L.A. resident Kardashian found that the long distance dynamic and their demanding schedules "made it really difficult to maintain a relationship."

Quizzed about the comic's energy after they paired up for a 2021 campaign shoot, the model raved during an appearance on Late Night With Seth Meyers, "I mean, he seems super charming. He's vulnerable. He's lovely. His fingernail polish is awesome. He looks good!" Plus, she summed up, he has a "super great relationship with his mom."So when the mama's boy reached out last November following his split from Kardashian and her breakup with husband Sebastian Bear-McClard, she decided it would be fun to catch up. As a source told E! News at the time, "Emily thinks Pete is a lot of fun to hang out with and they have flirtatious chemistry right now."Their love experiment continued for the next few weeks with the My Body author helping Davidson mark his 29th birthday. Still, an insider stressed that neither was looking to label their situation, calling it "a chill relationship." And by December she was heating up with designer Jack Greer.

Davidson got back in the game with his Bodies Bodies Bodies love interest, the pair spotted at a December 2022 New York Rangers game alongside costar Rachel Sennott before a January date night at Universal Studios Hollywood. The two "became fast friends on Bodies, and it was just clear that we could work together super well," she told Nylon in May. "He’s such a pro, and acting with him is my favorite thing." Which is why she signed up for round two, appearing on his semi-autobiographical Peacock series Bupkis as his on-again, off-again girlfriend.Off-camera, she continued, "We talk about everything and we are very open with each other about everything, and it feels like what's happening in our relationship is very sacred." But by late August, they were no longer feeling quite so blessed, multiple outlets confirming the couple had split.

Live from Las Vegas...the Outer Banks lead, who previously dated costar Chase Stokes, was first linked to Davidson in September 2023, when she flew to Sin City for the comedian's Pete Davidson Live standup show at the Chelsea, People reported. The pair called it quits less than a year later.

And while neither has shared exactly how their romance began, Davidson previously told Jon Bernthal on the Real Ones podcast, "These people that I've dated, I met them at work. I wasn't in anyone's DMs, no one was in mine."

Hewitt and Davidson were first romantically linked in March 2025 and announced they were expecting their first child together just four months later.

"Welp," the model captioned her Instagram post, "now everyone knows we have sex.”

The duo welcomed daughter Scottie Rose Hewitt Davidson on Dec. 12, 2025. The baby girl’s name paid tribute to Pete’s late father Scott Davidson, who died on 9/11 when the comedian was 7 years old.

However by May 2026, Elsie shared in a TikTok video that she was raising their daughter “on my own,” although a source confirmed to E! News at the time that, "Pete has been 100 percent present in Scottie’s life.”

The two reached a co-parenting agreement in August 2026 and even celebrated Halloween together later that year, with baby Scottie dressing up as Tony Soprano from The Sopranos.

#845. Germany news: Police raid chapters of Gremium MC biker gang

Police in southwestern Germany launched major early-morning operations against a biker gang. The state of Baden-Württemberg is outlawing three of its chapters. Meanwhile, unions are planning more strikes.

This blog is now closed. Read below for a roundup of news from or pertaining to Germany on November 12, 2026:

Luxury automaker Mercedes-Benz is halting investment at its facilities in Germany, a board members announced on Thursday.

Mercedes-Benz is "forced to examine, in concrete and detailed terms, which sites in Germany we can still afford to maintain," board of management member Britta Seeger said in an interview published on the company's intranet.

Germany's major IG Metall trade union has enabled the possibility of longer warning strikes amid difficult negotiations for industrial employees.

"The board of IG Metall has pave the way for 24-hour warning strikes in the metalworking and electrical industry," the union said on Thursday.

The union accuses employers of intransigence after three rounds of negotiations without clear progress.

On Wednesday, regional chapters appealed for authorization for full-day warning strikes — the last step before a full union vote and an indefinite labor dispute.

"This escalation is completely excessive and counterproductive," Udo Dinglreiter, the president of the employers' umbrella organization, Gesamtmetall, said. He said that hundreds of thousands of jobs could be at risk.

IG Metall's first chairperson Christiane Benner countered that "the employers want to turn this round of collective bargaining into a dispute over principles." Another union official said they were offering what amounted to a real-terms pay cut rather than seeking solutions.

IG Metall is calling for a 5% pay increase and other improved conditions for some 3.7 million workers starting in November, while employers have offered a one-off payment in 2027 coupled with a 1.3% increase starting in the summer of 2028.

The union estimates that around 464,000 employees took part in the initial wave of warning strikes that were limited to periods of hours, rather than full days.

Employers argue that they're treading a difficult line between trying not to cut jobs and meeting calls for improved pay amid widespread industrial sector layoffs in Germany in recent years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

'Tis the season, already. Preparations are underway around Germany and in several cities, Christmas markets are opening to the public.

Some markets are already open in Essen and in Hamburg, Duisburg's opens on Thursday, and Cologne's follows a day later.

The coupons.de website has sought to track the planned prices for mulled wine or Glühwein as the markets open their doors nationwide.

The bad news? These prices are rising like so many others. The better news? The year-on-year increase is actually smaller than overall inflation figures, at around 1%.

On average, a cup is liable to set you back around €4.60 (roughly $5.10). Not entirely surprisingly, Munich tops the nationwide pricing chart, with the price peaking at €7. Other sites nationwide tend not to have the gall even to charge 6 euros.

Bargain hunters determined to get the best value mulled wine will need to venture deep into the center of Germany — hardly its core tourist hub — to find the lowest prices starting at around €3.50.

Deposits for the cup, the "Pfand," are also only going in one direction, and in the meantime range from €1 all the way up to €5. But there's a strong argument, particularly with the better designs or after a memorable trip, that this can be money well spent as a memento!

Police in the Emsland region in the northwest near the border to the Netherlands have reported a major fire in a complex of residential and commercial buildings in Papenburg.

The fire broke out on Wednesday afternoon, police said the following morning, causing damages worth "at least €10 million ($11 million)." Several hundred emergency services personnel were deployed.

"Based on current findings, the fire broke out in the sauna area of a gym facility on site, and quickly spread to further parts of the complex of buildings," police wrote.

Two men were in the sauna at the time and initially tried to douse the flames but without success.

Police said the buildings were evacuated as the fire spread, with some surrounding buildings also being cleared as a precaution because of possible smoke-related dangers.

Several people were injured, police said, including the two men in the sauna area suffering mild burns and suspected smoke inhalation sickness. They were treated in a nearby hospital but soon discharged.

"There were also injuries among the first responders," police wrote. "Four police officers, two firefighters and members of the rescue teams suffered mild injuries, particularly via smoke inhalation."

The fire was only extinguished late on Wednesday night, several hours after it started. The area is sealed off, with possible risks of damaged buildings collapsing. Police have also launched investigations into the fire's cause, but said that at present, the area was not safe for that work to start at full scale.

Germany's largest credit bureau Creditreform has published its "2026 Debtors' Atlas."

It finds that 10.16% of German adults, or 7.36 million people, exhibit at least the early warning signs of excessive debt. A year ago the ratio was 9.74%.

"The financial situation of private consumers has further deteriorated," Patrik-Ludwig Hantzsch, Creditreform's head of economic research, said. "In particular, the sharply increased living costs, energy costs and housing costs are straining expenditures."

Hantzsch said employment was also becoming an issue once more, saying "above all, well-paid jobs in manufacturing industries have been cut back in large numbers in recent months."

The report also highlights rising cases of signs of excessive debt prior to legal action being taken, such as payment reminders or warnings being sent, saying "consumers are taking on more credit-financed expenditures — increasingly also for smaller purchases — at simultaneously rising interest rates."

A larger share of men than women have excessive debts, perpetuating a longstanding trend.

People around the middle of their working lives, aged 30-39 and 40-49, are most likely to be affected — but the cohort with the fastest-rising share of people with excessive debts are young adults below the age of 30.

Bremen, Berlin, Saxony-Anhalt and North Rhine-Westphalia were among the states with the highest rates of excess debts, while the wealthy and fiscally conservative states of Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg had the lowest levels.

Germany's main DAX stock market index has cleared the 27,000-point mark for the first time in its history in morning trading.

It climbed by around 1.3% in order to pass the milestone.

A combination of some positive outlook data from major companies, not least engineering giant Siemens, and the falling oil prices of recent days have helped fuel the uptick.

Siemens' shares had risen by almost 5%, to just over €291 (around $323) each, helping to spur on the gains and making the company the morning's top performer.

Despite several years of low growth and recession in the German economy, the DAX, like many Western indices, is now trading twice as high as it was prior to the COVID pandemic.

Hundreds of police officers searched apartments and meeting sites for the biker group "Gremium MC" in the southwestern state of Baden-Württemberg early on Thursday.

The state interior ministry said the operation was part of a move to outlaw three sub-chapters of the group, the ones based in Böblingen and Leonberg, as well as the "Gremium MC Chapter Nomads Bosphorus Türkiye."

This last group was highlighted as a meaningful part of Gremium MC by security officials. It describes itself on Facebook as a great example that "people of different cultures and faiths can be strong together," featuring images of men posing with knives and other weapons.

Gremium MC prominently incorporates into its iconography the symbol of the Prussian military medal for exceptional valor, the Iron Cross, which was discontinued after World War I, reintroduced by Adolf Hitler during World War II, and then scrapped for good.

State Interior Minister Manuel Hagel was expected to make further comments later in the day in Ludwigsburg.

Gremium MC is deemed an "outlaw motorcycle gang" in Baden-Württemberg's latest security report, a term used for biker groups that do not recognize the state monopoly on the use of force and are often tied to organized crime.

"Extortion, drug dealing and pimping in particular tend to be part of their activities," state authorities say.

Baden-Württemberg counts 154 biker chapters in the state with around 2,000 members.

Founded in 1972 in Mannheim, various chapters of Gremium MC across the country have faced legal issues in recent years. In 2021, another chapter in the southwest, Gremium MC Southgate in Heidelberg, was outlawed on suspicion of organized crime activity.

Police in Hanover reported early on Thursday that three men were injured by an unknown driver in a car in the nearby town of Ronneberg.

One person sustained severe injuries in the incident late on Wednesday, police said.

Two of the wounded were taken to a nearby hospital while the other could be cared for at the scene.

Police said the driver fled the scene and that a search operation was ongoing. Authorities were also still investigating a potential motive for the apparent attack.

Today's updates start with a focus between the southwestern Kurpfalz and Swabian regions, where police have launched major morning raids against a biker gang.

The state Interior Ministry in Baden Württemberg has outlawed three of its chapters. Hundreds of police officers mobilized in the early hours of the morning.

The major IG Metall trade union is planning further strikes in the carmaking sector and other metalworking industries, with an announcement anticipated later in the day.

To the north, near Hanover, police report an apparent car attack injuring three men overnight.

And in the spirit of offering the public service journalism people are truly thirsting for, we'll have some info on the average and localized pricing of mulled wine or Glühwein at Christmas markets this year, as the early birds start to open their doors to visitors. (Yes, already!)

Stay tuned for updates on all this and anything else of note in or pertaining to Germany as the day progresses.

#842. Summer signings join Lionel Messi among MLS’s top earners: Takeaways from the league’s salary release

How much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season? The latest batch of salaries lends some insight

Lionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Second-year LAFC forward Son Heung-min sits fourth on $11.2m.

Casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami announced his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. The MLS Players’ Association lists Casimiro on a base salary of $896,004.

All of these earnings figures were revealed as part of the MLS Players’ Association’s twice-a-year data dump, with the latter installment dropping hours before the league’s postseason commenced. While these figures don’t include transfer fees and therefore don’t tell the whole picture of a team’s investment in its roster, it’s a useful bit of insight in regards to how each team is spending on player wages.

Figures are players’ guaranteed compensation inclusive of base salary and all guaranteed bonuses; does not include marketing and other bonuses.

Thirteen of MLS’s 30 clubs have a new highest earner after a busy post-World Cup transfer window. Two – Anders Dreyer (San Diego, $3.6m) and Mateusz Bogusz (Houston, $2.5m) – rose to the top after the departure of a higher-paid teammate. Lozano overtook the injured Riqui Puig after arriving with the LA Galaxy on loan from San Diego. Lewandowski, Griezmann, and Embolo hold similar status, while Charlotte replaced Wilfried Zaha with Allan Saint-Maximin ($7.2m) earning nearly three times as much as the Crystal Palace great.

Other top-earners signed from beyond the league are Brais Méndez (Columbus, $5.2m), André Luiz (Kansas City, $3.3m), and Kai Wagner (Philadelphia, $1.6m). Two strikers who were traded within the league mid-season signed fresh terms that made them their new teams’ highest-paid players: Rafael Navarro (St. Louis, $4.95m) and Dejan Joveljic (Seattle, $3.7m).

The standout failure of the new big earners is Alexis Sánchez. The 37-year-old Chile legend came to North America this summer, joining CF Montréal and making 15 league appearances for the Quebecois club but failing to register a single goal or assist. His $2.97m guaranteed compensation makes up 24.6% of the team’s wage bill.

Griezmann’s arrival means that Messi no longer carries the largest share of any team’s wage bill, as Orlando has dedicated slightly more to the Frenchman (49.5%) than Miami has to the Argentinian (47.7%). Lewandowski narrowly trails by accounting for 47.3% of Chicago’s wage spending. Importantly, Messi’s contract includes add-ons; a portion of Apple TV subscriptions, merchandise sales through Adidas and Fanatics, and an optional ownership stake in Miami when he retires.

Other notable new wages include former Middlesbrough attacking midfielder Morgan Whittaker (Colorado, $2.0m), former Watford and Everton midfielder Abdoulaye Doucouré (Charlotte, $1.0m), former Manchester United left-back Tyrell Malacia (Cincinnati, $1.04m), former NYCFC playmaker Santi Rodríguez (Columbus, $3.9m), South Africa striker Lyle Foster (Houston, $1.8m), former Celtic striker Kyōgo Furuhashi (LA Galaxy, $1.1m), Tunisia winger Elias Saad (Nashville, $1.7m), former Leeds winger Jack Harrison (New England, $3.65m), Côte d’Ivoire winger Bénie Traoré (NYCFC, $2.5m), former Netherlands striker Vincent Janssen (Portland, $1.75m), Tunisia winger Elias Achouri (San Diego, $2.6m), Scotland goalkeeper Angus Gunn (San Jose, $1.6m), and Southampton loanee Damion Downs (St Louis, $1.6m).

While this exercise cannot confidently include every transfer fee paid, the timing of this year’s drop after the regular season’s end allows us to size up how teams spent on wages against the league table.

Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.

Does spending more equal success? There’s a degree of correlation there, but it’s not strong.

How valuable is it to get a point in MLS? In 2026’s wage economy, exactly $512,394.

#841. Kristen Doute's Fiancé Luke Broderick Leaves The Valley After Season 3

Kristen Doute's fiancé Luke Broderick is raising a glass to his appearance on The Valley after three seasons. As Doute put it, "That was the decision he made."

Luke Broderick is pumping the brakes on his reality TV career.

After more than two years of spotlighting the highs and lows of his and fiancée Kristen Doute's life on The Valley, the real estate agent is walking away from the Vanderpump Rules spinoff.

"I'll set the record straight," Doute told Page Six in an interview published Nov. 20. "Luke has decided not to film The Valley this season. It was a discussion that he and I had together, really just focusing on our family and Luke's mental health before we started production."

While she and Broderick—who share 16-month-old daughter Kaia—spoke at length about his choices for the show's future, she planned to support whatever decision he made.

"I really left it in his hands and said I would love for him to be a part of it, of course, but if it wasn't right for him," she explained, "then I wanted to be there to support that as well and that was the decision he made. So he gets to spend a lot more time with Kaia these days, which is wonderful."

The most recent season—which concluded in August—gave fans a front-row seat to the couple's relationship struggles, including sexual intimacy and communication, especially after welcoming Kaia.

"No secret, last season was very difficult for both of us," she added. "Two-and-a-half months after having Kaia, we started filming. I had a really difficult postpartum until Kaia was about 10 months old, and I think there was a lot of expectation versus reality as new parents that we didn't really know."

Although Bravo has yet to officially confirm a season four renewal, Broderick's exit is only the most recent cast shake-up. In fact, Danny Booko and Nia Sanchez are staying put in Santa Clarita.

"We're incredibly grateful for this experience," the couple announced on Instagram in September, "but our priority is protecting our peace and our family. We are fully committed to each other and our beautiful children."

Booko and Sanchez—parents to son Asher, 5, twins Isabelle and Zariah, 3, and Adelaide, 16 months—also raised a glass to their fans for all the love and support.

"We want to thank everyone for all the love and support you've shown us," the statement continued. "Thank you to Bravo and the team for everything. We are looking forward to what the next chapter brings."

As Doute and Broderick focus on the next chapter of their lives, keep reading for more unexpected TV show exits.

Gregg Sulkin, Wizards Beyond Waverly Place

In the Wizards of Waverly Place spinoff's shocking series finale, Selena Gomez's Alex Russo reunited with teen love Mason Greyback (Sulkin)—only to reveal a devastating twist.

Greyback revealed his character died during the August 2026 episode, then his ghost filled in the gaps on what Alex has been up to in the years since his passing.

"You have a whole other life, Alex," he told her. "You got married. You have a beautiful daughter. And she needs you. That’s the life that you’re meant to live. You have to go back."

The couple announced that the third season of The Valley will be their last following a tumultuous season during which Danny’s drinking habits were questioned and he was accused of acting inappropriately while drinking.

“We’re incredibly grateful for this experience,” Danny and Nia—who share son Asher, 4, twins Isabelle and Zariah, 3, and Adelaide, 15 months—wrote in their September 2026 statement shared to social media, “but our priority is protecting our peace and our family. We are fully committed to each other and our beautiful children.”

The OneChicago fanbase was shocked when news broke in July 2026 that Miñoso, who has portrayed firefighter Joe Cruz since the show debuted in 2012, would be leaving the NBC drama during its upcoming 15th season.

The world of fire and ice featured another gruesome casualty as Ser Criston Cole was killed in the Riverlands during the Game of Thrones spinoff's July 26, 2026, episode.

In July 2026, E! News learned that Hawkins—who has portrayed Officer Kevin Atwater since the NBC drama debuted in 2014—was leaving the show after 13 seasons.

The "It's Not Unusual" singer claimed he was fired from his coaching position after 13 seasons over "financial difficulty with insurance."

“To be clear, I did not want to leave The Voice as l love the show and really appreciate the audience. ITV made this decision—obviously a while ago, and I was told just recently," Jones wrote on Instagram in September 2026. "They are offering a much-reduced role where I would make an appearance but without being actually involved from the start, and I’m not thrilled about that."

E! News confirmed in July 2026 that Scott—who has portrayed Detective Vincent Riley since the the long-running NBC crime drama's 23rd season—would leave during show's upcoming 26th season.

The Paramount+ drama's season 19 finale, released July 23, confirmed the longtime star will not be returning for season 20 after his character Elias Voit was locked up in prison for a murder he took the blame for.

"It was hard to say goodbye," Gilford told Us Weekly of his exit. "It definitely was one of my favorite characters I’ve ever gotten to play and partially because what a gift. Every season I got to do a different side of this character. It wasn’t like I was just doing the same thing every year."

Days after West Wilson confirmed his Summer House exit, news broke that Amanda, who has been a main cast member of the Bravo series since season two, will also not be returning for season 11 amid the fallout from their bombshell romance.

After his secret love affair with Amanda Batula nearly destroyed the cast friend group dynamic following season 10, it was no shocker that West walked away from the scandal (and the series) in June 2026 just weeks before season 11 was set to start filming.

The Rookie's corrupt lawyer Monica Stevens was no novice when it came to escaping death. "She's escaped multiple assassinations," actress Bridget Regan recounted to TV Insider of her character's four-season journey, "and prison time and being thrown in a woodchipper."

So when the attorney met her end on an April 2026 episode, "I wasn’t surprised," Regan noted. "I thought, 'Fair enough.' She’s had an amazing run, four years on this show. I’m only filled with gratitude."

Whitney Leavitt, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives

After making her big break on Dancing With the Stars and landing a starring role in Chicago and Broadway, the Utah native announced season five of the hit Hulu reality show will be her last as she's moving on to other professional projects.

Dr. Samira Mohan is checking out of The Pitt. Actress Supriya Ganesh will not be returning for season three of the HBO Max drama, Variety reported in April.

The exit isn't so shocking to fans given that Ganesh's character has been planning to take on a new residency program at another medical center.

The crime procedural said goodbye to Director Leon Vance (played by Rocky Carroll) in a March 2026 episode, 18 years after the leader's debut in season five. During the 500th episode, Vance was killed in a shooting with a corrupt agent and welcomed to heaven by late Chief Medical Examiner Donald "Ducky" Mallard (played by Adam Campbell).

Mehcad Brooks shocked fans in 2025 when it was revealed he was leaving the NBC crime drama ahead of season 25.

Brooks, who joined the show in 2022, portrayed Detective Jalen Shaw for three seasons.

Kevin McKidd and Kim Raver, who have played Dr. Owen Hunt and Dr. Teddy Altman respectively for nearly 20 years, shocked fans with news that they are leaving the medical drama, with their final episode being the season 22 finale May 7, 2026.

Jenna Lyons, The Real Housewives of New York City

Jenna Lyons announced she will not be returning for The Real Housewives of New York City's 16th season.

"The rumors …..Are true," the former J. Crew Creative Director wrote on Instagram in November 2025. "I was grateful to be asked to join season 16 of RHONY 'as a friend of '- knowing my personal life was not really available to be filmed, we agreed that made sense."

The fashion icon—who joined the Bravo series for season 14 in 2022—explained that she later realized being a supporting castmember wasn't for her.

"And after thinking it through I have made the difficult decision not return to the show," she continued. "I would be the oldest and only openly gay woman on the show and feel like this is an opportunity for a new dynamic to emerge."

After nine seasons, the A-list realtor is done selling mega-mansions on the Netflix reality show.

“I’ve gotten to a place where I don’t need the show financially,” Chrishell announed in November via social media. “I’m lucky to have other forms of employment, because it’s no longer good for my mental health.”

Jax Taylor announced he will not be returning to The Valley for season three amid growing concern from fans about his behavior during the show’s second season.

“Right now, my focus needs to be on my sobriety, my mental health, and coparenting," the Bravo star—who is embroiled in a nasty divorce from estranged wife Brittany Cartwright—shared in July 2025. "Taking this time is necessary for me to become the best version of myself—especially for our son, Cruz.”

Michael Longfellow, Emil Wakim & Devon Walker, Saturday Night Live

The Saturday Night Live stars all announced within days of each other that they would not be returning for the sketch comedy series' 51st season.

Longfellow and Walker each spent three seasons on SNL while Wakim exited after just one season.

Heidi Gardner & Ego Nwodim, Saturday Night Live

Weeks after Longfellow, Walker and Wakim left SNL, longtime fan-favorites Gardner and Nwodim also confirmed they would not be returning for season 51 after eight and seven seasons, respectively.

Sofia Mattsson exited the long-running soap opera in summer 2025 after seven years playing Sasha Gilmore. Her character left Port Charles for Paris.

The Pitt star Tracy Ifeachor walked away from the hit HBO Max series after the medical drama's breakout first season.

"It was an absolute privilege to play Dr. Heather Collins in such a groundbreaking season and piece," the actress posted on Instagram July 10. "Thank you to everyone who has watched & supported Season 1 & shared their stories with me."

While fans maybe should have been aware that the days were numbered for Pedro Pascal's Joel Miller, considering his April 2025 death was quite similar to how it unfolded in The Last of Us Part II, the 2020 video game season two of The Last of Us is based on, the moment his character was brutally impaled still stunned.

Pascal, meanwhile, who also died onscreen in Game of Thrones and Buffy the Vampire Slayer, took his game over status in stride. "I get killed a lot," he joked to Entertainment Weekly. "I like to die."

After what he dubbed "one wild adventure," Peter Krause officially extinguished his role as 9-1-1's Los Angeles Fire Department captain Bobby Nash on an April 2025 episode of the procedural drama.

“Bobby Nash was written in sacrifice, and he was built for this,” Krause wrote in a statement to the Hollywood Reporter. “First responders risk their lives on the job so that others can see another day. His story arc honors them.”

Killing off the somewhat tormented, but beloved, firefighter was certainly a hot topic, showrunner Tim Minear acknowledged to Variety, "but after eight years, it just felt like, if we have any hope of creating stories going forward that have actual stakes, then someone's got to die."

Paige DeSorbo announced in June 2025 that she was walking away from the Bravo series after seven seasons.

"You’ve seen me grow up over these last 7 summers. I’ll always be grateful for the memories, the community, and the opportunities this wild ride has brought me," the Giggly Squad podcast cohost shared with fans on Instagram. "But like all good things (and some bad decisions), it’s time for this chapter to close."

The French actress confirmed she would not return for the hit Netflix series' fifth season in April 2025.

"After an incredible journey, I’ve made the decision to step away from Emily in Paris,” she wrote in an April 23 Instagram post, alongside pictures of her and her former castmates on set. “It has been a truly wonderful experience, one filled with growth, creativity, and unforgettable memories.”

Ahead of The Sex Lives of College Girls' third season, Reneé Rapp announced she would be leaving the Max series.

"College Girls moved me out to LA and introduced me to some of my favorite people," she wrote on social media in July 2023. "2 and a half years later—it's given me y'all and this community."

The show's co-creator Mindy Kaling also confirmed Rapp's exit. "We love @reneerapp so much and of course will be so sad to say goodbye to Leighton Murray!" Kaling wrote on her Instagram Stories before referencing Rapp's thriving music career. "We can't wait to see our friend on tour!!"

More than a year after Kevin Costner was rumored to have unexpectedly walked away from the hit Paramount drama after four and a half seasons, he confirmed in June 2024 that he will not return to finish out the series' fifth and final season.

After 19 years as Meredith Grey, Ellen Pompeo scrubbed in for the last time as a series regular on the ABC drama in February 2023.

"I gotta mix it up a little bit," Pompeo explained on The Drew Barrymore Show in December 2022, though she has already returned for a May guest appearance and continues narrating the series. "I'm 53, my brain is like scrambled eggs. I gotta do something new. You can't do The New York Times crossword puzzle every single day."

But she's not gone for good. Pompeo still pops in and out of Grey Sloan Memorial Hospital.

#839. Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’

Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham

The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one.

Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field.

Hayworth’s family was from Seville province. “I know she was a great actress but I’m afraid I have to admit I’m not one for old films,” García concedes in an even tone. “My uncles played rugby for Ciencias and practically all of them were in the national team together. They tried to get me to play with my cousins, but I was always more into football.” He was good at it too: another Spain international, the Club World Cup’s top scorer, playing for Real Madrid.

Then this summer, with opportunities limited, he joined Fulham, his introductory interview conducted in impeccable English. Having joined Madrid aged 10, he was leaving home for the first time, as Fulham’s record signing, at 22. He had the language and intelligence to embrace it. As for being uprooted, he was used to that, growing up in Argentina and Chile as well as Spain.

“From very little my parents impressed upon me the importance of study, learning languages,” García says. “I’m at Villanueva university [in Madrid]. I started with dual honours business and analytics, although that became difficult with my profession. Now it’s just business, and I’m trying to arrange with the university how best to handle it [from London]. My parents considered it fundamental to speak English and I was always at international schools.

“Every two or three years we would change city. Obviously, there would be phases when I felt: ‘Pfff, again?!’ Having to move home because of my parents’ work. But I look back and feel grateful because, seen with perspective, it gives you opportunities to meet new people, see new places, learn. I’ve always had foreign friends with whom I spoke English.”

García has been joined at Fulham by César Palacios and Manuel Ángel from Madrid’s academy. Three 22-year-olds, like your very own Erasmus course. “Nah,” García says, laughing. “I wouldn’t call it an Erasmus because we’re talking about a big, ambitious career step. We’re grateful for the trust placed in us. I’ve been pleasantly surprised by London, a huge city with people from all nationalities and cultures and Fulham fit the situation I was in, the desire to grow.

“Álvaro Arbeloa explained the project, convinced me. I’d worked with him in Madrid. He knows me perfectly, how far he can push me. Equally, I know what he wants of me. That helps … [Arbeloa] told me it was a project that it will take time but that he needed me. I’m very, very happy. It’s one of the world’s best leagues, if not the best.”

And the toughest? Is English football as wild as it looks? “Yes!” García replies. “They had told me it was demanding, hard, but …” He cracks up. “I have to admit it still surprised me. That first game against Chelsea, I finished really, really tired. It was box to box, intense, a lot of running. Bit by bit I’m adapting. The intensity and pace is very different.

“Spain is more tactical, a bit more technical. English football is pace. You can’t lose concentration for a second, not a second. Anything can happen any moment. How many Premier League games are decided late? Suddenly there’s a goal in the 90th minute and again on 93. It’s your corner and their chance. The level of concentration, that constant transition, is what most sets the Premier League apart.”

Despite defeat on that opening day against Chelsea, García scored. A superb goal followed against AFC Wimbledon in the Carabao Cup. “It was super special to do it at Craven Cottage. I love how close the fans are – they can reach out and touch you. But I don’t consider myself someone who’s easily satisfied. I’m not like that. I always want more, more, more.”

García hasn’t scored since and Fulham went five league games without a win, pressure building. Which is where the calmness comes in. By the time they faced Hull, Arbeloa appeared on the edge of the sack, questions asked about his signings, García especially. Were three Madrid academy kids really what Fulham needed? Was the coach’s relationship with them not such a good thing after all?

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

No player is impermeable to what is said, García admits, but he insists: “We treat that as outside noise. And we all knew that the beginning wouldn’t be easy. There’s a change of cycle: the coach goes, a new coach comes, there are signings, a different system, idea. Everyone has to adapt: those already at the club and those of us who are new. We’re young too. Results weren’t going our way but we had good intentions: to play good football, build, apply the manager’s ideas bit by bit. We had to remain calm.”

Fulham go into Saturday’s game at Manchester City unbeaten in four in the league, the sense of them shifting towards something more pragmatic not shared by García. “I don’t think we changed anything against Hull,” he says of a game Fulham won 1-0. “We didn’t do anything we weren’t already doing. Nothing. Maybe we controlled the small details that hurt us but the idea was the same. The players were very clear what the manager asked, very firm: it was just a question of time. You have to be patient. If you watch Fulham, you see the manager’s idea: have the ball, construct attacks well, show maximum intensity constantly with and without the ball. Aggressive, ambitious.”

Chances are coming for García but goals aren’t. He has started every league game but not scored or assisted since the opening day. Yet if there is a sense of a man feeling the pressure, that’s not repeated here; instead there’s an evenness, an ease. And a smile when another, more welcome, stat is raised: he has made more off‑the‑ball runs into the area than anyone. Something to hold on to, perhaps, a process that will pay off. “Really?” he says. “Well, I’m happy for people to see that a striker can help the team without the ball. In the end, it’s about following the manager’s instructions.”

In the end, though, teams will be judged on results and strikers on goals, price too. He knows: this is what he does, the path he chose. “Pressure depends on how you look at it, really,” García says. “Football is [very psychological]. It happens fast: it doesn’t give you time to enjoy good moments or linger on bad ones. It’s a rollercoaster – up there, down here. It’s not flat, but you maintain balance, work daily, improve: go in, focus, repeat.

“It’s not that I don’t ‘care’ about the price, it’s that the market is the market; it doesn’t depend on me. Calmness always, perspective … I know strikers are measured by goals but, well, the days I don’t score I’m completely sure I will be able to walk off the pitch and say that, no matter what happened, I helped my team, doing a load of other things. It is what it is.”

It is also time. A head peers around the door, the bus is going. García holds out a hand, apologises again. “It’s been a pleasure,” he says.

#838. Johnstone no longer need to play twice in one day

Johnstone Burgh won the Scottish Junior Cup, now the Scottish Communities Cup, two seasons ago

Scottish fifth-tier club Johnstone Burgh will no longer be forced to play two cup ties on the same day after one of the fixtures was postponed.

Johnstone were scheduled to play away to Tayport in the Scottish Communities Cup third round at 14:30 GMT and host Dunipace 65 miles away in the Lowland League Cup first round at 15:00 on Saturday.

However, the tie with Tayport has been called off because of a frozen pitch.

The double engagement came about after neither of Johnstone's opponents, nor any other clubs they were scheduled to play on other weekends, were willing to shift from Saturday afternoon kick-off times.

#837. What are fossil fuels?

They are in our shampoo bottles, power our cars and heat our homes. But what actually are fossil fuels, and why do they matter?

Whether in the form of crumbly rock, odorless gas or slick black liquid, ancient organic compounds have powered the flourishing of modern life. But now they threaten to make the planet unlivable for many plants, animals and humans.

The collective term refers to coal, oil and natural gas — a group of energy sources that contain carbon and hydrogen.

They started life hundreds of millions of years ago as living plants and animals. When they died, they sank to the bottom of oceans and swamps where they decomposed under layers of sediment.

Over time, this matter was buried deeper and deeper into the earth, subjecting it to increasing pressure and heat which changed its chemical composition. Plants and trees transformed into coal, whereas microscopic plankton and algae became oil and — if the heat and pressure increased further — gas.

Today fossil fuels can be found in the earth's crust all around the world although some countries, such as the US, Saudi Arabia and Russia, have bigger reserves than others.

Coal, found in underground coal beds, is extracted by mining, whereas oil and gas, found in reservoirs beneath the land and ocean, are accessed by drilling.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Since the early 19th Century, when the discovery and exploitation of fossil fuel reserves powered the Industrial Revolution, our use of them has skyrocketed, increasing eight-fold since 1950.

Today they provide 80% of our energy needs through heating, electricity generation and transport.

We transform them into energy either by burning them directly in furnaces that warm up our homes and businesses, or in power plants to heat water into steam which then generates electricity. When it comes to transport, crude oil is refined into a range of products such as diesel, gasoline and kerosene that are burned in the engines of automobiles, airplanes and ships. Natural gas is also sometimes compressed for use in cars and buses.

But fossil fuels are also essential to a huge range of products including steel, formed using a coal-derived material called coke, and plastic, which is produced by refining and processing crude oil and gas.

Fossil fuels are by far the biggest contributors to climate change. When burned to power our modern lives, they emit carbon dioxide (CO2) into Earth's atmosphere, trapping heat and causing temperatures to rise.

With 2025 officially one of the warmest years on record, the impact of these emissions is being felt around the world. Hotter temperatures are causing polar ice caps to melt and creating the conditions for extreme weather events — such as floods, drought, wildfires and storms — to become more intense and frequent.

Scientists stress the need to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) to avoid unleashing the most catastrophic impacts of climate change. That was laid out in the 2015 Paris Agreement. Currently, there are 194 parties to the agreement, but progress has been too slow, and overall emissions continue to rise.

Three years after countries agreed at the UN climate conference in Dubai COP28 to transition away from coal, oil and gas. After the previous COP in Brazil failed to reach a consensus on a concrete plan, Brazil has now presented a roadmap aimed at turning that promise into national plans.

"It is long past time to stop treating the transition away from fossil fuels as taboo or intractable," United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said.

#836. Jennifer Lawrence Reacts to Connor Wood Comment Going Viral

After Jennifer Lawrence playfully called out DWTS season 35 contestant Connor Wood for paying her “no mind,” despite naming her as his celebrity crush, she reacted to the quip going viral.

Jennifer Lawrence was paying no mind to what the internet would think of this quip.

After The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping actress playfully called out Connor Wood for ignoring her when they once crossed paths, she admitted she didn’t think it would get so much attention.

“I don’t really know how to feel about it,” Lawrence told Andy Cohen during a Nov. 19 appearance on Watch What Happens Live alongside costar Josh Hutcherson. “I did not expect that to go viral. I don’t really get it.”

Lawrence—who joined Instagram in September—dropped the now-viral comment last month on a clip of Wood sharing she was his celebrity crush, and he wanted her to notice him.

“I just want a little acknowledgment from Jennifer Lawrence that I’m funny,” he said in an Oct. 20 Instagram video. “And that’s all I need.”

He joked, “Jennifer, I really need something good to happen to me.”

To which Lawrence revealed he’d already had his chance in a comment that now has over 100,000 likes, “I saw you on 8th avenue drinking a smoothie and you paid me no mind.”

Wood later reacted to the comment in a video shared by his Dancing With the Stars season 35 dance partner Rylee Arnold.

“‘I saw you on Eighth Avenue drinking a smoothie and you paid me no mind,’” Wood read over and over in the video. “It’s rolling around in my head.”

As Wood neared tears in the video, Arnold assured, “Don’t be upset! She’s doing that to be funny.”

Later, the 31-year-old embraced the comment, stepping out in a T-shirt with the quote emblazoned on the front, as well as striking up a brand deal with Smoothie King.

While the moment has inspired memes and even merchandise, it didn’t go viral for everyone. As Hutcherson joked during WWHL of the ordeal, “I don’t know what any of those words mean.”

Lawrence, meanwhile, had one correction to make. It wasn’t Eighth Avenue after all. As she noted, “It was also Greenwich.”

#835. OL Lyonnes show their class to hit Arsenal’s ambitions for a top-four WCL finish

Arsenal’s hopes of earning automatic progression to the Champions League quarter-finals were dashed by OL Lyonnes, as the French side continued their statement form in Europe.

Goals in either half from Jule Brand and Melchie Dumornay were the ­difference at Meadow Park and Lyonnes are joint-top of the table and still yet to concede in the league phase with one game remaining.

It feels like Lyonnes are playing with a fire and intensity fuelled by their loss to Barcelona in May’s Champions League final. They look a more formidable, coherent and hungry side on a mission to end a four-year run without lifting the trophy they won eight times in a 12-year period between 2011 and 2022.

“We are already at a better level for sure,” said the Lyonnes manager ­Jonatan Giráldez. “Sometimes you just need time. We had nine new ­players last season and I was new too as the coach. I think we have improved the rhythm of the game and have identified positions better and are staying more compact. The most important thing is speaking the same language in possession and out possession.”

The visit of the eight-time ­European champions was always going to be challenging for the ­Gunners and based on current form getting a result would be even tougher. Last season’s runners-up had scored 20 goals without conceding in their first four Champions League matches prior to their trip to Borehamwood and scored 49 in their nine Première Ligue games.

The lack of competitiveness in the France top flight also meant they were able to rotate heavily at the weekend between their two European games. Giráldez made 11 changes for their 1-0 defeat of Saint-Malo on Saturday before returning to his first-choice lineup against the 2025 Champions League winners.

Clàudia Pina scored a hat-trick as Barcelona thrashed Servette 6-0 to go top of the Women’s Champions League standings. While Lyon were winning 2-0 at Arsenal, Barça edged clear at the top on goal difference as they dismantled their Swiss visitors.

Aitana Bonmatí fired in the opener in the 19th minute and then turned provider for Pina to drill home her first goal.

Esmee Brugts headed in a third in the 32nd minute, and Barça had their fourth just after the hour, with Caroline Graham Hansen hitting an emphatic penalty after Bénédicte Simon fouled Brugts.

Pina got her second in the 77th minute and tucked in from Brugts’s pull-back to complete her hat-trick late on.

Bayern Munich are two points behind after cruising to a 4-0 win over Austria Vienna. Klara Buhl headed the visitors in front after 27 minutes before Pernille Harder doubled the lead in first-half stoppage time.

Alara Sehitler’s stunning strike made it 3-0 with 15 minutes to go before Sophie Proost added a fourth in stoppage time.

Sofia Jahnukainen struck in stoppage time as Roma snatched a 3-2 win away to Benfica. Kayleigh van Dooren twice put the Italians in front, but her first goal was cancelled out by a thunderbolt from Caroline Møller, with Flourish Sabastine equalising after her second.

Paris FC got their first win of the competition, beating HB Køge 2-1 thanks to Célina Ould Hocine’s late penalty. Catherine Paulson fired the visitors in front 10 minutes in, but Sheika Scott bundled in a rebound to bring Paris level before the break. Press Association

Arsenal were not afforded the ­luxury of an easy league match after their battling 1-1 draw against ­Barcelona last week, playing a critical and tricky game against London City Lionesses, which also ended 1-1. Renée Slegers made two changes to the team that hosted ambitious London City, with Ona Batlle ­having picked up a knock Taylor Hinds played at left-back and Kyra Cooney-Cross started ahead of Kim Little.

They had their backs against the wall at a bitterly cold Meadow Park, as Giráldez’s galacticos controlled the game. The away team had almost 69% possession in the first half and amassed 12 shots to Arsenal’s one.

The surprise was that Lyonnes were not further ahead at the break, with Brand’s 24th-minute goal the difference, the full-back sweeping in Vicki Bècho’s ball from the right.

Brand was back to haunt the ­Gunners, having scored in both legs of last season’s semi-final between the two teams, with the French side progressing to face Barcelona in the final with a 4-3 aggregate win.

No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football

Arsenal were better after the break, but Lyonnes soaked up brief spells of Arsenal pressure, Marie-Antoinette Katoto the only player left forward as they banked back and crowded the box to give the home players few options.

They increased their margin and dampened the mood soon after Arsenal’s brightest period, Tabitha Chawinga’s cross from the left was collected by Katoto and the France forward laid the ball off for Dumornay who took a touch before powering the ball into the roof of the net.

It was an emphatic and unstoppable finish from one of the best players in the world as a mist lowered over the pitch.

“Congratulations to Lyonnes, they were better than us today,” said Slegers. “If you look at the block we’ve had, the challenges we’ve had with the run of games – ­Liverpool and Barcelona away, ­London City who are among one of the top teams in the WSL right now and Lyon, who are even better than last year – it’s a lot of games against strong teams with a short turnaround because Lyon were better than us.”

Arsenal need to quickly move on, with West Ham their last game before the international break. They had needed a win to have any serious chance of earning a place in top four, avoiding a quarter-final playoff place.

They now sit eighth and will face Inter in their final league phase match in December, with the Italians needing a win to keep any hopes of a playoff place alive. That will not be easy, but a seeded playoff place is in Arsenal’s hands, if they want it.

#834. Legendary Irish League manager Coyle dies aged 80

Coyle won 13 Irish League titles during an astonishing coaching career

Roy Coyle, the most successful manager in Irish League history, has died at the age of 80.

Coyle won 13 league titles during his 32-year managerial career, achieving periods of sustained success with Linfield and Glentoran.

He also managed Ards, Derry City and Newry City and had a spell as Glentoran director of football.

In a statement, Glentoran said the club were "deeply saddened to announce the passing of Roy Coyle, our former player and manager and one of the greatest figures in our history".

"A league champion in Glentoran colours, Roy went on to become the most successful manager in the club's history. His association with the Oval spanned more than half a century," their statement continued.

"His teams gave supporters some of their most treasured days, while his influence on players and colleagues endured long after his years in the dugout.

"To generations of the Glentoran family, he remained simply 'The Gaffer'."

A minute's applause was held in Coyle's memory before Glentoran's Irish Premiership game against Cliftonville on Friday at Solitude.

Watch: Roy Coyle reflects on legendary Irish League career

Belfast native Coyle moved into management at the age of 29 when he was appointed player-manager of Linfield in November 1975.

A midfielder during his playing days, Coyle had spells with the Glens, Sheffield Wednesday, Grimsby Town and Linfield after starting out with Ballymena United, and he also won five caps for Northern Ireland.

During his 15 years as Blues boss, Coyle won 31 trophies, guiding the club to 10 league titles in just 12 seasons, alongside two Irish Cup successes and an All-Ireland crown in 1981.

"Everyone at Linfield Football Club is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of former player and manager, Roy Coyle," the club said.

"His remarkable achievements and contribution to one of the most successful periods in Linfield's history will forever be recognised and remembered.

"The thoughts and deepest condolences of everyone at Linfield Football Club are with Roy's family, friends and all who knew him at this sad time."

After his contract was terminated by Linfield in 1990, Coyle had a spell in the League of Ireland with Derry City between two stints at Ards.

In 1997, he took over at Glentoran and transformed their fortunes, leading the east Belfast club to three league titles and four Irish Cups.

Coyle went on to become the most successful in Glentoran's history, winning 17 trophies before his nine-year tenure at the Oval came to an end in 2006.

He had a brief period in charge of Newry City and also returned for three spells as caretaker boss of Glentoran before retiring in 2017.

Coyle retired from management in 2017 after his third spell as Glentoran interim manager

Glentoran chairman Colin Jess paid tribute to Coyle, who was inducted into the club's Hall of Fame in 2025.

"Roy was one of the greatest figures in Glentoran's history, and his passing is a profound loss for our club," said Jess.

"He gave generations of supporters some of the happiest days of their lives. People will always remember where they were and who they were with when his teams won those championships and cups. That is a wonderful thing to have given so many people.

"He set high standards and earned lasting respect. His former players continued to call him The Gaffer long after their playing days had ended, and that says so much about his influence and the place he held in their lives."

Jess added: "We will miss seeing Roy at the ground, enjoying his company and talking football with him. It is difficult to imagine the Oval without him.

"Our deepest sympathy goes to Abbie, the whole family and all those closest to Roy. We are immensely grateful for everything he gave Glentoran, and we will remember him with great affection and pride."

Glentoran owner Ali Pour described Coyle's contribution to Glentoran as "extraordinary".

"He helped make the club champions as a player, led it through years of success as manager and continued to serve it long afterwards," added Pour.

"I often asked Roy for his advice on matters at the club. He knew Glentoran so well, and I valued his judgement and hearing how he saw things. I'll miss those conversations.

"The pride with which supporters remember his teams, and the affection his former players have for him, show how deeply his work mattered to people.

"We owe Roy a great debt of gratitude. His achievements are an enduring part of Glentoran, and we will ensure that future generations understand what he gave this club and why he meant so much to it.

"My family and I extend our heartfelt condolences to Roy's family, friends and everyone mourning his loss. He will always have an honoured place at the Oval."

Northern Ireland Football League (NIFL) chief executive Gerard Lawlor said Coyle's contribution to football in Northern Ireland "went far beyond the trophies he won".

"He was a man who dedicated so much of his life to our local game, earning enormous respect across the football community, regardless of club loyalties," their statement continued.

"Roy represented the passion, commitment and pride that make Irish League football so special. His passing marks the loss of one of the great characters and personalities of our game, and his legacy will live on for generations."

Coyle, who started his playing career at Glentoran, won five caps for Northern Ireland

Coyle lifted the Irish Cup four times as Glens boss

#833. US science academy urges journals to fix errors more quickly

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

A statue of Albert Einstein holding a scientific manuscript sits outside the US National Academy of Sciences building in Washington DC.Credit: Paul J. Richards/AFP via Getty

Science publishers take too long to retract or correct research papers, a report by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine (NASEM) finds. Standards for fixing errors are also inconsistently applied across research journals, it says.

Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science

Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science

There are no data on how long retraction or correction currently takes, as journals do not generally disclose when they were alerted to a problem in a paper; the NASEM report says they should. On average, according to the Retraction Watch database, retractions occur around 2.4 years after a paper is published. The report recommends that editorial review processes be completed within 12 weeks for most cases and should rarely stretch beyond 6 months — at least when editors are looking at concerns over a single paper.

“The big picture is, the process is too slow,” says Randy Schekman, a cell biologist at the University of California, Berkeley, who chaired the 14-person committee that produced the NASEM report. A prompter and more transparent process would strengthen the reliability of the scientific record, he says.

The report was due to be published online on 19 November, but publication was delayed after journalists at Science noted that it contained some references with fabricated first names for authors, a possible sign that large language models had been used to write or edit the material and had been insufficiently checked.

“It's unfortunate that there were these flawed references in a report about fixing the literature,” says Jennifer Byrne, a cancer researcher and research integrity sleuth at the University of Sydney who first flagged the concern to Science when reviewing the report, which was shared ahead of publication with media outlets.

The report had two main aims: to speed up the process of retraction or correction and to lower the “tremendous emotional barriers” for authors to correct honest mistakes in the record, Schekman says. “Part of the problem is that it’s too rare for a paper to be retracted,” he adds.

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

The report also suggests that journals shouldn’t just wait for complaints to reach them, but instead “take proactive steps” to identify errors and integrity issues. That might include journal-wide audits, or regularly monitoring social media and online platforms where post-publication issues are raised, it says.

Existing guidelines for publishers, such as those from the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) in London, only urge a “timely” response to concerns without setting out expected schedules, and don’t suggest journals scan online platforms for complaints.

“A major theme running through the report is that we have to distinguish between retraction or correction, and research misconduct,” notes Dorothy Bishop, a research-integrity sleuth in Oxford, UK, who was on the NASEM committee. Authors shouldn’t associate retracting a paper with the stigma of misconduct, she says. And although journal editors sometimes wait for a university to investigate whether there is research misconduct before correcting a paper, they shouldn’t, she adds.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a new record

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a new record

Calls for changing these attitudes aren’t new: journals have long emphasized that retractions can cover honest mistakes. When it comes to journal processes, Holden Thorpe, the editor in chief of Science, urged that issuing corrections or retractions and making a determination of misconduct be separated in an editorial in 2022, and COPE guidelines already emphasize the point. But “there are still plenty of people who see a correction or retraction as an allegation of fraud,” says Thorpe, who was also on the NASEM committee. “Hopefully, this report will accelerate the recognition of the distinction,” he says.
