#815. UK court convicts 2 Iranian men of spying on journalists

A London court has found two Iranian citizens guilty of surveilling reporters for a Persian-language television station critical of Iran's government. One was also convicted of planning a violent attack against them.

Two Iranian men were found guilty of spying on dissident journalists in Britain on behalf of Iran's Revolutionary Guard on Thursday.

British counterterrorism police said the case reflected intensifying hostile Iranian activity in the country, an issue that recently made headlines amid the security scare at the RAF Fairford airbase that's a major operational site in Europe for the US Air Force.

The men, both in their 40s, were arrested last year, with Iran repeatedly rejecting the allegations against them.

The Woolwich Crown Court in London convicted one of the Iranian citizens not just of spying on journalists working for the Persian-language dissident TV channel Iran International, but of plotting a violent attack against one or more of them.

The second individual had also faced charges of plotting an attack but was only convicted of spying on the reporters.

One of the convicted defendants said he was acting under duress after his family was threatened, and the other said he did not know that his actions were assisting Iranian intelligence.

A third defendant, a 57-year-old Iranian man, was acquitted of all charges.

The men were accused of engaging in conduct likely to assist the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Iran's multi-discipline military force that's seen as closer to the country's religious leadership and more influential than its regular armed forces.

The UK formally designated the IRGC as a threat to national security in July, meaning that supporting or assisting the organization can carry penalties of up to 14 years in prison as part of new rules on national security and state threats.

Sentencing in this case is still pending and is scheduled for mid-December.

"This was a calculated operation to spy on those critical of the Iranian regime," said Frank Ferguson, chief prosecutor for the Crown Prosecution Service's special crime and counter-terrorism division.

The two men were accused of visiting addresses linked to their targets, taking photos and videos, and using platforms such as ChatGPT to research them online

"Thankfully, the defendants were stopped before any attack could take place," prosecutor Ferguson said.

Senior ‌National Coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing Vicki Evans said that the IRGC or "middlemen" for Iranian intelligence were directing the plot.

Iran's government had repeatedly denied the allegations, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying he was "disturbed" by the trio's arrests last May.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

There have been four cases targeting the Persian language television channel Iran International since late 2023.

In July, two Romanian men were jailed for stabbing a journalist outside his home in 2024.

A spokesman for the broadcaster's parent company, Volant Media, said in a statement that Thursday's verdicts "don't make the lives of our journalists any safer so long as the Islamic Republic of Iran continues its campaign of death threats and violence against them."

Iran International reported that a British barrister was also one of the targets.

British law enforcement has been warning of an uptick of hostile Iranian activity in recent years, particularly since the US military operations against Tehran began earlier this year.

Most notably, the UK has accused Iran of being behind a suspected plot targeting the RAF Fairford base in September, after which US President Donald Trump withdrew some long-range bombers from the site.

Three men were indicted in the US in relation to that plot this week, while two others currently face charges in the UK.

But beyond this, the head of Britain's MI5 domestic intelligence agency Ken MacCullum said in October that Iran-linked operations had led to more than 50 arrests in the last year. He also said known cases of so-called state threats had more than quadrupled in a decade.

Counter-terrorism police chief Evans said she expected this trend to continue.

France this week also accused Iran of being behind a cyberattack targeting refrigeration units at hundreds of supermarkets in October, although Iran denied any involvement.

European governments are on heightened alert for so-called hybrid warfare tactics, from Russia as well as Iran, amid the geopolitical tensions of recent years. New technologies like low-cost drones and AI are also threatening to make such activities cheaper, harder to trace, and potentially more effective.

#814. Key questions as Scottish Premiership returns

Wouter Wrancken under pressure; Mario Frick's beginning; John McGlynn the saviour

The Scottish Premiership returns with an all-action Saturday after what was a bleak international break for the national side.

Most of the intrigue is on men who will not make a pass or a tackle. There is one new manager, one who is being touted for the Scotland job, another who has turned around a failing side and one who is increasingly under pressure.

And none of those are in charge of Old Firm teams. The managerial status at Celtic and Rangers is relatively settled, but of course that can change in the space of 90 minutes.

This is your essential guide to Saturday's action.

Aberdeen have a new head coach for their basement battle with Kilmarnock, with Mario Frick replacing Stephen Robinson

The Liechtensteiner was a fine striker in his day and his main mission is to get the Dons firing in front of goal again.

Frick favoured two up top while in charge of Luzern, so he needs to find a way to supply Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua.

Connor Ronan could hold the key to improving a sorry set of attacking statistics, but the Irish midfielder will need to show more than he has since his summer arrival.

Aberdeen have 12 goals from 12 league games. Kilmarnock have 13 from 13. Both sides have amassed just four points from their past six outings, so this may well be something of a scrap.

Killie were slightly more menacing in a 0-0 draw at Pittodrie in September and the same could be said of a League Cup quarter-final at Rugby Park a week later, although the Dons did well to prevail on penalties after a red card early in the second half.

The Ayrshire side have the league's worst defensive record by a distance, conceding three or more goals on six occasions. However, manager Neil McCann will have been heartened by a tenacious showing in the 1-0 loss at Celtic Park last time out.

With four successive matches coming against sides currently in the bottom six before taking on the Dundee duo, McCann will view this pre-Christmas sequence as vital.

Hear from Aberdeen's Mario Frick at first press conference

Of the leading sides, Celtic have the easier-looking task at home to St Mirren, who have enjoyed just one victory in their past 40 visits to the east end of Glasgow in all competitions.

However, the league leaders have not kicked on since thrashing Heart of Midlothian last month, drawing with Dundee United and losing to Falkirk either side of narrow and unconvincing wins over Hibernian and Kilmarnock.

That 1-0 win at home to Killie was just a second clean sheet in seven Premiership matches for the champions.

Celtic came from behind to win 2-1 in Paisley in September, with Yang Hyun-Jun grabbing the second. The winger's return should add dynamism to their attack.

Since pushing Celtic all the way at home, St Mirren have picked up a mere four points from nine matches.

Rangers go to Motherwell off the back of a 2-0 win away to the Buddies, extending their unbeaten league run to 10 games and maintaining the best defensive numbers in the table.

The goals came from a contentious penalty and a deflected shot and manager Derek McInnes spoke of the need to sharpen up in the final third after several promising situations broke down.

After a six-game losing slump that began in Govan, Motherwell have steadied the ship and played out an entertaining 1-1 draw with Dundee United before the break that included a combined 40 efforts on goal.

Well shared the points with Rangers at Fir Park last season, scoring late on both occasions, and, while not the force they were after so many departures, still retain a core of players who celebrated victory at Ibrox in April.

Rangers have the momentum, although recent draws away to Dundee and Hearts underline the fact they remain a work in progress under McInnes.

New manager Frick to take Aberdeen back to basics

We'll only sell if offer makes club blink - McInnes

Five wins on the spin have propelled Falkirk up to third place and they will be big favourites to extend that run at home to St Johnstone.

Celtic beaten, Hearts hammered... fans are talking about European qualification, having ended a five-year stint in League 1 in May 2024.

John McGlynn continues to work his magic on a meagre budget, with new arrivals Jacob Murrell, Owen Eames, Finley Barbrook and Deniss Melniks hitting the ground running.

Ethan Ross is lapping up a new lease of life, while older heads Scott Bain and Liam Henderson have never been better, although the loss of influential skipper Brad Spencer is a huge blow.

The Perth Saints will be no pushovers. They too are punching above their weight with just four defeats in 13 on their return to the top flight.

Rangers are the only side to beat Simo Valakari's men since a 1-1 draw with Falkirk at McDiarmid Park in mid-September.

That was the first league meeting of the clubs since 2010, but, with such astute managers in place, it looks like this can remain a top-flight rivalry for a good while yet.

Have Hibs turned a corner and have Hearts fallen down a hole?

Marink Reedijk lost his first three games after replacing David Gray, but now the Hibs head coach is looking for a third successive victory at home to Dundee United.

The Easter Road side clambered out of the bottom spot in style, thumping Aberdeen 4-0 at Pittodrie after coming from behind to stun their Edinburgh rivals in the League Cup semi-final.

Hearts went into that game at Hampden as heavy favourites and across the following seven days were outplayed by the team sitting eighth in the Swiss Super League and walloped by Falkirk, ending their 19-month long unbeaten home record in the league.

A growing injury list has hampered Hearts, but Wouter Vrancken's methods are being questioned, with only Kilmarnock conceding more goals in the league.

A visit to Dundee is next and Steven Pressley's much-improved team have only been defeated once at Dens Park so far.

United have also been a breath of fresh air, adopting a new swashbuckling style that has yielded four wins and four draws in their past nine games.

Hibs have taken significant strides, particularly in the midfield area, but this will be a real test of their progress. There were 11 goals in the two games against United at Easter Road last season and another big score would not be a surprise.

#813. Mowbray support no surprise, says interim boss Johnson

Tony Mowbray started his managerial career with Hibernian

The overwhelming support from the world of football for Blackburn Rovers boss Tony Mowbray has come as no surprise to interim head coach Damien Johnson.

Mowbray announced on Wednesday he was stepping back from his role at the Championship club because of health issues with Johnson and Mike Dodds taking charge "for the time being".

The news sparked an outpouring of messages of support from EFL clubs and further afield.

"To someone like me, it's not a surprise," Johnson said.

"I've known him for over 10 years, but I think people who have only known him in this club for the four or five months he's been in, they can see that. That's just the impact Tony has on people, it's just a testament to Tony and his nature and how he is and how he treats people."

Mowbray, 62, returned to Ewood Park in June for a second spell as head coach and has taken them to 13th place in the Championship after they finished just five points clear of the relegation zone last season.

The former Middlesbrough and West Brom boss had previously taken time out of the game during his spell as Birmingham City boss in early 2024 following a health scare, and later revealed he had been undergoing treatment for bowel cancer.

Boro head coach Kim Hellberg was one of the first to send his best wishes to one of his predecessors.

"He's a brilliant guy. It was really good to meet him and he was absolutely brilliant every time I've talked to him," Hellberg said.

"He's a brilliant football coach. He's done a lot of good things. He's a brilliant human being and you can see everyone knows that."

Rovers have won five of their past nine league games with Johnson crediting Mowbray's impact at the club for creating a more positive atmosphere.

"When the statement came out there was concern - we care a lot about Tony and it was a little bit of a shock - we want what's best for him at this time," Johnson told BBC Radio Lancashire.

"He sent a private message to the players which was read out today [Friday] and they appreciated it. He's sent some private messages to staff but Tony's allowed us just to get on, he'll be allowed the time he needs and we'll just get on with the game."

Blackburn visit Burnley on Sunday (12:00 GMT) hoping to end a 10-game winless run against their Lancashire rivals, who have not won a home game in the league since 18 October last year.

Johnson says the match is their main focus rather than what may happen with the managerial situation down the line.

"We've just been focused fully on the game, we know it's a huge game and we've been working with the team throughout the week. The discussions have been about the game and nothing else," he added.

Meanwhile, Blackburn are set to be without goalkeeper Balazs Toth until the new year after he told Hungarian media, external he suffered a hand injury while playing for his national side against Northern Ireland on Tuesday.

"The situation is not that good, but for now it looks like I will be able to avoid surgery," he said before travelling back to England to have the injury assessed by Blackburn.

#812. Melania Trump Reveals Warning She Gave Son Barron Trump About Dating

President Donald Trump’s wife Melania Trump detailed the dating advice she gave their son Barron Trump, noting it’s a “dangerous world” so he should “be careful.”

Melania Trump is a special adviser for her son’s dating life.

The First Lady recalled the cautionary advice she gave her and President Donald Trump’s 20-year-old son Barron Trump when it came to his romantic life.

“I always say it’s a dangerous world out there,” Melania said in the Nov. 20 episode of her new Prime Video docuseries MELANIA, “and be careful.”

And beyond his dating life, the 56-year-old noted she’ll be there for Barron “anytime he wants to have my advice or input.”

“We have very open communication regarding life. I will always be there for him,” she continued. “I am, and I will always be. And he knows that he’s my priority, and he will always be my priority.”

Plus, as Melania quipped, “I'm a very cool mom to Barron, and I remind him all the time."

But while the former model has prioritized motherhood, she has been vocal about not strutting the path of parenthood alone. That’s why she was grateful to have her late mom Amalija Knavs, who died in 2024, to help raise Barron.

“My mother was the epitome of love and warmth, and for Barron, a grandmother who filled every moment with joy and wisdom,” Melania told USA Today in May. “Every story she read to Barron sparked his imagination, and every game they played strengthened their bond.”

Now, the Melania author is passing down the hard-earned advice she gained from raising Barron.

“To all the young mothers out there: Shower your children with love and support and always communicate openly,” she continued. “See them as their own unique individuals, not merely as extensions of yourself.”

And when it comes to ensuring a bright future for the next generation, Melania added, “Guide them with wisdom but establish a foundation of freedom where they can carve their own life path.”

For a closer look at the branches of Melania’s family tree, keep reading…

Ivana Trump was the first wife of President-elect Donald Trump. Born in Gottwaldov, Czechoslovakia—now Zlín of the Czech Republic—in 1949, she rose to fame as a competitive skier. And, thanks to her marriage to Austrian ski instructor Alfred Winklmayr in 1971, Ivana was able to travel often outside of Czechoslovakia.According to her book Raising Trump, the model met Donald three years after her 1973 divorce during a New York trip, where she'd traveled for a Canadian fashion show ahead of the Montreal Olympics. They wed in 1977 and welcomed three kids: Donald Trump Jr. born in 1977, Ivanka Trump born in 1981 and Eric Trump born in 1984.The pair's divorce was finalized in 1992 following his affair with Marla Maples, whom he later married. However, Ivana—who then married Riccardo Mazzucchelli for two years followed by Rossano Rubicondi for less than a year—and Donald remained on good terms.“Donald during the divorce was brutal,” she told ABC News in 2017. “He took the divorce as a business deal, and he cannot lose. He has to win. So he took about two years. And after the final situation was straightened up, we would just talk and we are friends.”Ivana died in 2022 at age 73. According to NBC News, the New York City Medical Examiner said she died of “blunt impact injuries” and that her manner of death was an accident. A senior NYC official with direct knowledge added the circumstances were consistent with a fall on the stairs in her New York apartment.

In 1977, Ivana and Donald welcomed their eldest son Donald Trump Jr. He graduated with a Bachelor’s degree in finance and real estate from the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School in 2000 and began working for his father’s company The Trump Organization in 2001, where he now serves as the executive vice president. Don Jr. is also a director for both Trump Media & Technology Group Corp and PublicSquare Holdings and part of 1789 Capital firm. In addition, he's been involved in his dad’s political campaigns, including speaking at rallies and the Republican National Convention during his father's presidential runs.Don Jr. shares five children with his ex-wife, model Vanessa Haydon: Kai (who also made a speech at the 2024 Republican National Convention) Donald III, Tristan, Spencer and Chloe.Don Jr. was previously engaged to Fox News alum Kimberly Guilfoyle. However, he recently confirmed their split."Kimberly and I will never stop caring for each other," he told Page Six Dec. 13, "and will always keep a special bond."Don Jr. has since been linked to socialite Bettina Anderson. As for Vanessa, she is dating Tiger Woods.

Four years after the arrival of Don Jr., Donald and Ivana became parents to daughter Ivanka Trump. Before her father’s presidency, the University of Pennsylvania alum worked at The Trump Organization. But after he was elected in 2016, the fashion brand founder—who had her own eponymous line—took on the role of Advisor to the President.After her dad announced he would be running for president again in 2024, Ivanka revealed she would be stepping out of the political arena to focus on her family with husband, former White House senior advisor Jared Kushner, and their children Arabella, Joseph and Theodore. “I love my father very much,” she said in part of a 2022 statement obtained by NBC News. “This time around, I am choosing to prioritize my young children and the private life we are creating as a family. I do not plan to be involved in politics.”

Born in 1984, Eric Trump is the third child of Ivana and Donald. He graduated with a degree in finance and management from Georgetown University.Like his brother, Eric works as executive vice president of The Trump Organization, which he joined in 2007. He is also president of Trump Winery.Eric is married to Republican National Committee co-chair Lara Trump, with whom he shares kids Luke and Carolina.

Marla Maples is Donald’s second wife, whom he met while still married to Ivana.

In Raising Trump, Ivana wrote the actress approached her about the affair during a trip to Aspen in 1989. Still, Marla said on a 2018 episode of the ABC podcast Journeys of Faith with Paula Faris that she “never considered” herself a mistress. "My intention was to never bring hurt," she continued. "Do I wish more than anything that we could have had this relationship after his divorce papers were signed? Absolutely. I mean, with all my heart. How much heartache would it have saved so many people if I had seen that piece of paper before we got involved? But it didn't happen that way." Marla and Donald welcomed daughter Tiffany Trump in 1993, and the couple wed later that year. However, the Dancing With the Stars alum and the 47th commander in chief announced their separation four years later and finalized their divorce in 1999.

After her parents’ breakup, Tiffany Trump relocated with her mother to California. "She moved us out of New York to get out of the spotlight and let me grow up and find my own identity versus being in the shadow of a name or growing up very young with all that pressure,” Tiffany told People in 2016. “So, she wanted me to have a chance to have a normal childhood. As normal as possible. I think that she did well in that.” She released her 2011 single “Like a Bird" and graduated from the University of Pennsylvania in 2016 with a B.A. in sociology, focusing on law and society. She then went to Georgetown Law School, where she graduated with a JD in 2020. In 2022, Tiffany wed Michael Boulos. Her father announced they're expecting their first baby during an October 2024 speech at the Detroit Economic Club. "She’s an exceptional young woman," he said during his remarks. "And she’s going to have a baby. So that’s nice.”The little one made his debut on May 15, 2025."Welcome to the world our sweet baby boy, Alexander Trump Boulos," Tiffany wrote on X on his birthday. "We love you beyond words! Thank you for coming into our lives!"

Melania Trump is Donald’s third wife and current First Lady of the United States. Born in Mesto, Slovenia in 1970, she is the second First Lady to be born outside of the U.S. and the only First Lady to become a naturalized U.S. citizen.Melania met Donald in New York in 1996 while she was working as a model. “It was a big fashion party that my friend organized, fashion week, and he invited me,” she recalled on a 2016 episode of On the Record With Greta Van Susteren. “That’s how we met with Donald.” Melania and Donald married in 2005, and they welcomed son Barron Trump the following year. In 2024, she released her memoir Melania and she's set to appear in a documentary. Melania has also spoken about where she will spend her time during her husband's second presidency.

"I will be in the White House," she told Fox & Friends in an interview that aired Jan. 13. "When I need to be in New York, I will be in New York. When I need to be in Palm Beach, I will be in Palm Beach. My first priority is to be a mom, to be a first lady, to be a wife. And once we're in on January 20, you serve the country."

Born in 2006, Barron Trump is Donald and Melania’s only child. While he has lived a more private life—relocating with his parents from New York to live in Washington, D.C. and then Florida—it looked like he might enter the political world after he was selected in May 2024 as a Florida delegate to the Republican National Convention. However, Barron declined the offer."While Barron is honored to have been chosen as a delegate by the Florida Republican Party,” a statement from Melania’s office shared with NBC News at the time said, “he regretfully declines to participate due to prior commitments.”Like studying, perhaps, with Barron starting his freshman year at New York University in 2024. "He was accepted to a lot of colleges," his father told the Daily Mail in an interview published Sept. 4. "He's a very smart guy, and he'll be going to Stern, the business school, which is a great school at NYU."However, Melania told Fox & Friends in her interview that Barron will come and visit his family at the White House, and he was there for his father's inauguration ceremony in January 2025.

#810. Sutton's predictions v world champion boxer Lauren Price

Manchester United start life under new boss Mauricio Pochettino on Sunday but will they get their first Premier League win since August when they face Liverpool at Anfield?

"My worry for United is that they have one of the worst back fours in the Premier League," said BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton.

"Their defensive record is something Pochettino will try to address but, whoever he picks, they are just not very good."

Sutton is making predictions for all 380 Premier League games this season, against AI, BBC Sport readers anad a variety of guests.

For week 11, he takes on boxer Lauren Price, who is an Arsenal fan.

She will defend her unified welterweight titles against Michaela Kotaskova on Friday, and has a shot at becoming Wales' first undisputed world champion after the vacant WBO welterweight title was added to the fight.

Price returns to home soil at the Utilita Arena in Cardiff for a fight that will be shown live on BBC Two and BBC iPlayer, from 21:00 GMT.

Do you agree with their predictions? You can pick your own below.

The most popular scoreline selected for each game is used in the scoreboards and tables at the bottom of this page.

A correct result (picking a win, draw or defeat) is worth 10 points. The exact score earns 40 points.

Want to make more predictions? You can play BBC Sport's new Match of the Day predictor game every week, featuring six fixtures from domestic and European competition.

Price, the first Welsh boxer to be an amateur world champion and win Olympic gold, said: "When I turned pro it was my dream to become 'undisputed'. To achieve that and make history again for Wales on Friday, and in front of my own fans too, would be a dream come true."

Before turning to boxing, Price was a world kickboxing champion and international footballer - she captained the Wales Under-19 side, and played for the senior team as well as Cardiff City.

"My football days have helped me massively to get where I am in the ring today," the 32-year-old told BBC Sport.

"I honestly believe my footwork, and how fast my feet are, comes from when I played football.

"I am really proud of everything I achieved in football, especially playing for my country. It is the same now in boxing - to get in the ring and represent Wales is always an honour."

Price said the support of her grandparents helped her become successful at so many sports - and she followed her grandad, Derek, by becoming an Arsenal fan too.

"When I was a kid I was absolutely besotted with football and Arsenal were THE team when I was growing up," she explained.

"It was just the way they played under Arsene Wenger, and how they passed the ball - it was incredible. I loved Robin van Persie but Thierry Henry was my icon, my hero."

Chris Sutton and Lauren Price were speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

The AI predictions were generated using Microsoft Copilot Chat - we simply asked the tool to 'predict this weekend's Premier League scores'.

The wheels have come off for Enzo Maresca at Manchester City with three Premier League defeats in a row.

It's not just City's results which have been alarming, either - they were well beaten by Nottingham Forest last time out, and their performance would have been the biggest concern for their manager.

In contrast, Fulham's results have improved of late and they are unbeaten in four league games. They've done all right whenever I've seen them this season, so I'm not surprised to see them picking up points.

Still, the international break probably came at a good time for Maresca to sort things out. Erling Haaland is scoring again too - not that he ever really stopped for very long - and I'm expecting City to be much better here.

I'm even going for them to keep a clean sheet, for the first time in eight games. I'm always brave... which is why I am bottom of the predictions table.

Lauren's prediction: City are having a tricky time of it at the moment but they should still win this. 2-0

I was at Sunderland's win over Chelsea and they thoroughly deserved it. They had been on a dreadful run of results before then, but it was a reminder of what they are about.

Brian Brobbey was just phenomenal for the Black Cats in that game but, like his captain Granit Xhaka, he is injured and will miss out here.

That just makes me think Aston Villa will have the edge. I always fancy them at home anyway with the way they go after teams, although I don't think this will be easy for them.

Villa boss Unai Emery was fuming after his side threw away a two-goal lead twice in their 4-4 draw at Manchester United, but they will hold on this time while Sunderland go down fighting.

Lauren's prediction: Villa are going really well. 2-1

Bournemouth have won eight games in a row in all competitions and it is incredible how Marco Rose has turned things around after a slow start.

The Cherries were absolutely flying before the international break - but will the two weeks off affect their momentum?

Forest did not need the break either, after their brilliant win over Manchester City.

That was such an important result for their manager Oliver Glasner but I think they will find it difficult to follow it up at Bournemouth.

Lauren's prediction: Forest shocked City last time out but I am going with Bournemouth here, they are on a brilliant run. 2-1

Chelsea were so lethargic when I watched them lose against Sunderland, and I don't think they were hard done by in that game - they looked flimsy at the back, and were deservedly beaten.

I had a bit of a pile-on from some Chelsea fans for saying that after the game, but then Xabi Alonso came out and was also heavily critical of the way they had defended - so he and I are on the same page there.

If Joao Pedro is fit then they will at least have more physicality up front this week, but I still have a feeling Leeds will get something out of this.

Daniel Farke's side got a great win over Tottenham last time out and they do not give much away - Arsenal and Brighton are the only top-flight teams to have conceded fewer league goals this season.

Leeds have definitely benefited from signing keeper James Trafford and what a move it has been for him personally as well.

I admire him for that, because he could have hung around at Manchester City as Gianluigi Donnarumma's number two, but he wanted first-team football. Now he is battling it out with Jordan Pickford to be England's number one.

Lauren's prediction: I don't think Leeds will keep Chelsea quiet. 3-1

This is the battle of the Franks... Lampard versus Thomas.

Thomas Frank's first conundrum as Crystal Palace's new manager is to stop them leaking so many goals - they have conceded 24 in their first 10 games, which is concerning.

I still think Palace have got some really good players, like Ismaila Sarr, Jorgen Strand Larsen and Jean-Philippe Mateta, and it's just a case of them getting fit and finding some form.

The way Coventry play, the Eagles are going to get some chances - but can they take them?

Frank Lampard's side counter-attack with such vigour, so I definitely think they will score... but I can see Palace's forward players having some joy too.

Lauren's prediction: I'm standing next to a Palace fan now, Ed from Boxxer, so I've got to go with them here! 0-2

We've seen Palace change their manager after making a disastrous start but they are still only four points below Ipswich and they will certainly see that as retrievable.

The Tractor Boys are not in the relegation zone but they are still in a relegation fight so, it is important for them to keep picking points up here and there. The trouble for them is that I don't see them getting anything at Tottenham.

Spurs lost to Leeds last time out but I still think they have turned a corner with their performances before that defeat.

I actually think this will be a routine win for Roberto de Zerbi's side, and I'm going for them to keep a clean sheet too.

Lauren's prediction: Spurs will take this one. 2-1

I am covering this game and I think it is a huge one for Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle.

The Magpies have picked up as many points - 12 - in their first 10 games under Jaissle as they did when Eddie Howe was in charge last season, but I still don't think their fans are overly convinced by him.

Some of their unease is because Newcastle don't seem to have a defined style of play, and can be a bit kamikaze going forward.

Because of that, I just think Arsenal will pick them off, and win comfortably.

The Gunners have conceded only five league goals so far and have made an incredible start to their title defence with nine wins out of 10.

The worry for their rivals is that it feels to me Mikel Arteta's side have not even got going yet, but I still don't see anyone being close to them.

Lauren's prediction: No problems for Arsenal here! 0-4

Hull are going to scrap and fight - they have not won for eight games now, but they have still picked up some points because of their battling approach.

You know they will get in Brighton's faces but I don't think it will bother the Seagulls too much.

I want to apologise to Hull fans because I keep writing the Tigers off every week, but I am going to do it again here because Brighton are such a good team going forward and defensively.

Lauren's prediction: Brighton to edge this one. 0-1

Good luck to Pochettino. I like him as a manager and he seems a decent guy too.

He will need some luck as well, because it is going to be incredibly difficult for him to succeed at Old Trafford.

The constant for Manchester United is their managers keep getting the sack, when the club's problems seem to be deeper-lying than that.

Pochettino will get time because of what he has taken over, but it is amazing and also alarming to think United are in the bottom three, and could be bottom by the time this game is played.

As well as being so poor at the back, they have a midfield without any great athleticism and, stylistically, they did not really have an identity under Michael Carrick.

If you are Pochettino, you are probably going into the dressing room and putting your arm arm around Bruno Fernandes, to get the old sulker onside.

He really needs to, because Fernandes is an outstanding player and played a key role in the club's form with his numbers last season.

United need to see that version of him more than ever now, because so far this season he has not got going at all.

As for Liverpool, well I think they will get there under Andoni Iraola. It is just taking a bit of time for his players to adapt to his style.

They are not particularly fluid most of the time, and it feels like Iraola is not quite sure what his best midfield is.

Liverpool are still a work in progress, and United have picked up some results at Anfield recently - two draws and a win in their past three visits - but I can only see one result here, and it is a home victory.

Pochettino will probably look to defend and play on the counter-attack, and they might get some chances that way, but Liverpool are going to win. The only question is how many they will score.

Carrick began by beating Manchester City and Arsenal in his first two games in January. Pochettino might start by being on the wrong end of a pummelling.

Lauren's prediction: Liverpool are at home and I am going with them to win it. 2-1

Brentford beat Everton 4-2 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium last season but, in three of their past four meetings, the points have been shared.

This has got a draw written all over it, too.

Everton are so solid under David Moyes, and so well organised, that I just don't see them losing. Brentford will keep things tight as well.

Lauren's prediction: Both these teams are doing well and this should be pretty even - I haven't gone for a draw yet, so let's finish with one. 1-1

#808. Sleuth finds ‘impossible proteins’ in hundreds of research papers

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Some studies show the expression of proteins such as caspase-3 (pictured), in cell lines that should not be able to produce them. Credit: Dr Mark J. Winter/Science Photo Library

A scientific sleuth has identified more than 220 research papers that describe impossible patterns of protein expression in genetically altered cell lines. In these studies, particular proteins show up in imaging experiments, even though the cells do not have the gene necessary to make them.

Journals are now taking action to clean up the literature by retracting or correcting the work, and researchers warn that there are probably many more affected studies.

“This problem will not go away,” says Thierry Soussi, a cancer geneticist at Uppsala University in Sweden, who notes that there are several other examples of the issue in now-retracted papers that were not included in the sleuth’s analysis. “This is only the tip of a gigantic iceberg.”

Cell lines are groups of cells derived from a single origin cell and cultured for use in experiments. Some cancer cell lines have been genetically modified with mutations and deletions — often to remove genes that usually control cell division. This means that the cultures continually divide and grow, giving researchers the chance to study tumour progression and test potential treatments.

The MCF-7 cell line is one of these. It lacks the gene for caspase-3 protein, which is involved in cell death. In 2009, researchers warned1 that some studies that report working with MCF-7 have mysteriously observed caspase-3 expression in western blots, an imaging technique that identifies proteins based on their molecular weight.

Sleuth identifies dozens of studies that used the wrong antibody

Sleuth identifies dozens of studies that used the wrong antibody

In the most recent analysis, published as a preprint on 21 October to the data repository Zenodo2, Sholto David, a sleuth based in Arbroath, UK, finds that this problem persists and extends to other cell lines.

David compiled a list of 20 commonly used cell lines with genetic mutations or deletions that leave cells unable to express specific proteins. He then scoured the literature using Google text and image searches to identify examples of western-blot images that unexpectedly identify these proteins. He also searched a collection of 140,000 articles that he had previously downloaded and screened for image-integrity issues and other problems, most of which were biomedicine papers.

He found 230 reports of phantom proteins across 221 papers published since 2004. The most common errors were observations of caspase-3 expression in the MCF-7 cell line, affecting 49 papers; expression of the cell-death protein BAX in the Jurkat cell line in 47 papers; and expression of the signalling protein STAT3 in the PC-3 cell line in 35 papers.

David suggests several explanations for these impossible protein-expression patterns. They might be the result of honest errors: researchers could have misidentified the cell lines or contaminated them with others. Or the antibodies used to identify proteins in the western-blot experiments could have been non-specific and bound to another protein with the same molecular weight. In fact, David says that he stumbled across the anomalous proteins while working on a project that flagged hundreds of studies that used the wrong antibodies in experiments.

Another possibility is that some of the papers are the product of papermills, companies that fabricate and sell scientific manuscripts. David says that some papers in the cache contain the hallmarks of being produced by such outfits, including duplicated images or text templates that are similar to other papers. The proportion of the papers that fall into this category is not clear, he says.

Nature has contacted several authors of papers containing anomalies to ask for comment, but none responded.

#807. Golloria Responds to Huda Beauty’s Apology for Removing Darkest Powder

Beauty influencer Golloria responded to Huda Beauty founder Huda Kattan's apology for how the company handled removing its darkest setting powder Coffee Cake and replacing it with Coco Truffle.

Golloria can’t conceal her thoughts on Huda Beauty’s apology.

After the makeup brand’s founder Huda Kattan apologized to the beauty influencer for how her company handled discontinuing their darkest setting powder Coffee Cake and replacing it with Coco Truffle, Golloria shared her thoughts on the response.

“I appreciate your apology and you taking the time to get back to me,” Golloria posted in the comments of Kattan’s Nov. 20 Instagram post. “Speaking from both my experience as a shade consultant and as a dark skinned woman whose shade options are directly affected by this decision, I don’t think Coco Truffle should replace Coffee Cake. And that’s just the honest truth.”

The TikToker explained that she heard Huda Beauty’s reasoning that Coffee Cake wasn’t doing well with consumers, but added that she didn’t think the two shades were “interchangeable,” noting that “a shade occupying a similar depth in a range doesn’t necessarily mean it serves the same complexions.”

“You’ve said several times that you want to better serve dark skinned women, and part of that is listening to the women telling you that Coffee Cake already works for them,” the 25-year-old continued. “That feedback should help guide what you preserve as you expand the range.”

She also added that darker skinned women “deserve variety in both depth and undertone,” and that having both shades would help create that inclusion. Instead, Golloria shared in her own Instagram caption that she felt Huda Beauty was “doing what's easiest for the brand instead of what's needed by the women you say you want to serve.”

“Inclusion means making room for our differences,” she wrote, “not asking us to settle for whatever is most convenient for you to offer.”

As for Kattan, while the beauty founder did not reply to Golloria’s comment, she explained in her apology video that she was sorry for how the conversation about the shade replacement had been handled with Golloria, especially as it was happening during a busy time for the brand and when Kattan herself had to undergo emergency surgery for a ruptured breast implant in April.

According to the 43-year-old, her team found that Coffee Cake was “not something that a lot of people have shared positive feedback with us on,” adding that they “definitely thought we could make it a lot better.”

The decision led them to launching Coco Truffle as a replacement for Coffee Cake, first as a pressed powder, then as a loose powder—although it was not yet widely available.. But after hearing from their consumers, Kattan realized they should have done a better job being more inclusive with their shades.

“Inclusivity is not about, ‘Yes, done, check, we're inclusive.’ That to me is some of the things that are wrong with the industry,” she said. “It's 2026. We can do better. We can do better and I think brands should be doing better in 2026.”

And while they will be reworking Coco Truffle to make sure it’s available “as quickly as possible,” she also regretted fully removing Coffee Cake from their lineup.

“We should have kept it in stores,” Kattan said, “because at the end of the day, if some people liked it, we should have kept it in stores until there was something better available.”

She also once again apologized for not having better communicated all of this to Golloria initially, although she was hopeful that the beauty influencer and Huda Beauty fans would appreciate Coco Truffle.

“I'm hoping to give you guys a shade that you guys really, really love, and all the beautiful rich skin tone girls and boys feel really represents them,” Kattan shared, “and is perfect for their skin tone.”

#806. Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul

The reforms mark a break the the conservative policies of former PM Viktor Orban. The controversial "heartbeat regulation" is to be scrapped and women are to be better protected against violence.

Hungary on Thursday said it would ease abortion rules and ratify an international treaty on violence against women.

Under the planned changes to the so-called "heartbeat regulation," women will no longer be forced to listen to the vital signs of the fetus before an abortion.

Women will also be able to get emergency contraceptive pills without prescription.

The changes proposed by the new government under Prime Minister Peter Magyar are a significant break with the conservative policies of his predecessor Viktor Orban.

The country also plans to ratify the Istanbul Convention, a treaty aimed at preventing violence against women and domestic violence.

Hungarian law allows for most abortions to be performed up to 12 weeks, and up to 24 weeks in cases of severe developmental abnormalities. Until now, women were required to have a medical provider show them evidence of a definitive sign of fetal life, commonly understood as the so-called "fetal heartbeat," before deciding whether to have an abortion.

The controversial 2022 policy had received widespread criticism from doctors and women’s rights groups as being cruel and humiliating. It will now be scrapped.

The policy had not led to a decline in abortions and according to Magyar, had raised "serious bioethical questions."

The second major change is that emergency contraception will be available without prescription.

Further measures include changing the criminal code aimed at better protecting women, including making the misuse of intimate images a criminal offense and strengthening the treatment of victims of domestic violence during criminal proceedings.

Hungary also plans to ratify an international treaty on the protection of women which most other EU members have long ratified. The Istanbul Convention came into force in 2014 and, among other things, requires rape to be criminalized based on the absence of freely given consent.

"We are making it clear that sexual acts can only ⁠take ​place with the voluntary consent of the other party," ​Magyar said.

The government of his predecessor Orban had opposed the treaty, arguing that it promoted what it described as "gender ideology."

"We are making a clear and accountable commitment to putting an end to the era of inaction," Magyar said in a Facebook video.

Among the EU’s other members, only Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Lithuania and Slovakia have not yet ratified the convention.

The Istanbul Convention is a treaty by the Council of Europe, an international organization that promotes human rights and the rule of law across Europe and includes more countries than the member of the EU.

#805. Inside the rise of 'humble' Nyoni and why Iraola trusts him

Trey Nyoni scored his first Liverpool goal earlier this month

Trey Nyoni knew this was the season when opportunity beckoned for him at Liverpool.

With Curtis Jones leaving for Inter Milan and the club deciding not to buy another midfielder, Nyoni saw the prospect of regular first-team action if he impressed new head coach Andoni Iraola in pre-season.

First impressions matter. So on the day he returned from a holiday in Morocco in June, Nyoni went from the airport to a personal training session in Leicester - where the 19-year-old grew up and where his family are still based.

Nyoni sought the help of a private football coaching operation as he targeted off-season gains before joining up again with Liverpool.

Coach Steve Stavrou and his son Emillio have also worked with players including Harvey Barnes and Haji Wright. Nyoni asked to work on line-breaking passes, getting away from pressure and improving his finishing.

"We merely supplemented the ability he's already got. He's a quiet and humble lad but knows his ability on the pitch and plays with such a confidence," Emillio Stavrou tells BBC Sport.

Under Iraola, Nyoni has thrived after a stellar pre-season, making 13 appearances already, just one shy of his total appearances last season.

Earlier this month, he scored his first goal for the club in Istanbul.

Liverpool ultimately lost to Fenerbahce in the Champions League that night and Nyoni's belief that "the night has been ruined" showed his inner competitiveness.

His first Premier League start came against last season's champions Arsenal on 1 November.

Nyoni fouled Arsenal's captain early on, leading one source to remark: "He's a nice kid but you saw that steel too with the way he went into Martin Odegaard."

Perhaps the most significant praise came from Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard, who said he couldn't see why Iraola was taking Nyoni off just before the hour mark in that game.

Iraola was managing Nyoni's workload, with the midfielder playing 85 minutes three days later in Turkey.

By now, it is clear that Iraola is unafraid to use him.

"He has to continue in the same place he has been since pre-season: being ready for every game. He is playing all the games lately - so we trust him," said Iraola.

That speaks volumes of Nyoni's rise since joining from Leicester City in 2023 and making his Liverpool debut under Jurgen Klopp as a 16-year-old.

Nyoni, whose parents have Zimbabwean heritage and support Liverpool, is in advanced talks over a new deal.

Having made his England Under-21 debut last week, this is turning into a breakout season with club and country.

Under Iroala, Nyoni has made six starts for Liverpool

In the summer window, the average spend on a player signed from another Premier League club was Â£39.4m.

Judging by Liverpool's recent signings - the likes of Alexander Isak (Â£125m), Bradley Barcola (Â£123m) and Florian Wirtz (Â£116m) - there is a sense of satisfaction at the club when the likes of Rio Ngumoha and Nyoni, who cost a fraction of those sums, emerge as first-team options for years to come.

A tribunal decided that Liverpool had to pay Chelsea up to Â£6.8m in compensation for Ngumoha. In Nyoni's case, Liverpool paid just under Â£1m in compensation to Leicester.

Nottingham Forest were linked with a Â£30m move for Nyoni in the summer. Forest denied making the bid, while Liverpool were not interested in a sale.

Iraola saw enough over pre-season to know the teenager would play a prominent part in the new campaign. He only got 237 minutes last season under Arne Slot but has already played 619 minutes this time around.

Slot saw the potential of Nyoni, who trained regularly with the first team. But, given Liverpool's struggles in 2025-26, the Dutchman was reluctant to experiment.

Under Iraola, Nyoni is finding his feet in a deeper midfield role than he had been used to, seeing more of the ball.

"I've been playing like a number six. I played there when I was young, but it's a new position for me. I've had to learn a lot in a short space of time," Nyoni told The Inside Scoop., external

The time he spent before pre-season impressed on the coaches there what a talent Nyoni possessed.

"In the drills, he'd make everything game realistic. Everything was with intent and you see a lot of what he does is with disguise, particularly with his passes," Emillio Stavrou recalls.

With two games a week now the norm for Liverpool, Iraola will continue to rotate his team.

But seeing who he names in midfield against Manchester United on Sunday will be interesting because Nyoni is showing that he can fight for a position alongside the likes of Dominik Szoboszlai, Ryan Gravenberch and Alexis Mac Allister.

Inevitably there is work to be done, particularly in terms of endurance and physicality, in order to cope with the rigours of playing consistently at the top level, but it is so far, so good for Nyoni.

Liverpool and Man Utd fans give predictions ahead of Premier League match

In a similar manner to Ngumoha's emergence last season, Liverpool were keen not to block Nyoni's pathway, and under Iraola he has been given the platform to thrive.

Liverpool are still only an injury away from looking short of options, so getting another midfielder remains a priority for next summer.

Monaco's Lamine Camara and Bournemouth's Alex Scott are two players of interest.

In the here and now, Nyoni needed this opening. He has come out of his shell and feels a lot more like a part of the squad. That quiet nature is slowly changing and that was visible in an interview he did while on England duty.

Asked how Liverpool are doing by one of the hosts, who supports Manchester United, Nyoni simply responded: "Better than United."

Deep down, there is a young man that backs himself and by all accounts, loves football. Neymar is his favourite player.

"He's obsessed with training and obsessed with getting better. The first session we had with him after he'd just got off the plane tells you about him," adds Emillio Stavrou.

Nyoni told Stavrou's little brother in the summer that he backed himself to play regularly for Liverpool.

'Future is really bright' for 'revelation' Nyoni

Nyoni set to make it 'difficult' for Iraola

#804. Pochettino’s fiery start, plus England v All Blacks and ATP Finals finale – follow with us

Here’s how to follow along with our coverage – the finest writing and up-to-the-minute reports

The international break is over as domestic football boogies back. Primed to feel the force is Dominic Booth at the helm of our essential gateway to the weekend’s action. Saturday offers a magnificent seven Premier League matches, bookended by Manchester City v Fulham and Newcastle v Arsenal. There is also a full programme of Championship, League One, and League Two fixtures, plus Celtic and Rangers taking to the Glasgow greensward in Scotland. In the WSL, Liverpool host Chelsea before rich kids London City prepare to receive Crystal Palace. For breaking news, reader input and good vibes aplenty – join the conversation at matchday.live@theguardian.com.

To the background buzz of Australian cricket ripping itself apart over sandpapergate, England kick off their T20 series at the same venue they became world champions four years ago. The Melbourne Cricket Ground has not always been a happy hunting ground for touring England sides but Harry Brook’s last two visits as captain have been triumphant. A two-day win at the 90,000-capacity venue in last year’s Boxing Day Test was not only the high point of a traumatic Ashes campaign; it was their first red-ball victory on Australian soil since 2011. MCG also hosted England’s T20 World Cup triumph in 2022, where Brook was part of the side that defeated Pakistan to lift the trophy behind enemy lines. Rob Smyth has over-by-over coverage with Ali Martin reporting from Melbourne.

The lunchtime kick-off is a vital one for the hosts. City have wobbled of late, three straight Premier League defeats leave the beleaguered club in third with 21 points from the first 10 games of Enzo Maresca’s tenure. In stark contrast, the Cottagers are unbeaten in their last four games, after four defeats and two draws in their first six. Wins over Hull and Coventry came before draws with Aston Villa and Newcastle. Barry Glendenning helms the blog as Will Unwin reports from the Etihad Stadium.

England are have been transformed since stumbling through the Six Nations and then falling to South Africa at Ellis Park, winning four consecutive Tests, amassing 36 tries and addressing their disciplinary lapses. Aided by thumping victories over Fiji and Japan, they have rebuilt impressively to secure a shot at reaching the Nations Championship final, but New Zealand provide the true measure of their progress. Only South Africa are higher in the rankings and a year out from the 2027 World Cup final, it is the opportunity for Steve Borthwick’s men to make a statement. Lee Calvert blogs the action and the trio of Robert Kitson, Andy Bull and Gerard Meagher making up our Twickenham reporting team.

Katy Murrells is at the controls of our tennis liveblog as the semi-finals pan out in Turin. The first session starts at 2.30pm, with the evening match due to start at about 8.30pm.

Emillia Hawkins keeps the updates flowing on the five afternoon kick-offs: Aston Villa v Sunderland, Bournemouth v Nottingham Forest, Chelsea v Leeds, Coventry v Crystal Palace, and Tottenham v Ipswich – the pick of the bunch. Roberto De Zerbi seemed to be making an impact at Spurs before a defeat by Leeds tripped up his side. Their record is grim against the Tractor Boys: four defeats in their last five Premier league games.

Lee Calvert is back on deck as Ireland risk a Springbok backlash from a side bruised by defeat by France and furious at their coach, Rassie Erasmus, for getting banned after his incendiary “match-fixing” comments. There is more at stake in this November’s meeting between the sides than last year’s chaotic Test. The Irish were down to 12 men at one stage and the Springboks won 24-13 for their first win in Dublin since 2012. Both countries are still in the running to top their respective pools and play in the final on Finals weekend at Twickenham. Brendan Fanning reports.

City’s slump has allowed the defending champions, Arsenal, to seize early control and they will hope to continue their relentless start to the season. They head to Newcastle where a toxic reception awaits Bruno Guimarães as he returns to Tyneside in Arsenal colours for the first time since his summer move. The Gunners are five points clear of second-placed Brighton at the top after winning nine of their first 10 games. Matthias Jaissle’s inconsistent hosts have managed just one win in their past five league matches, losing to Everton and Aston Villa along the way. Join Rob Smyth for MBM commentary, with Louis Taylor reporting.

Kimi Antonelli may have already won the drivers’ crown, but second place in the standings is still up for grabs and Max Verstappen can tighten his grip in Sin City. The Red Bull driver is 17 points clear of Mercedes’ George Russell, who moved back up to third place, one point ahead of Lewis Hamilton after his fourth place at Interlagos. Krishani Dhanji be live blogging the race in the small hours, with Giles Richards reporting from Las Vegas.

Dominic Booth and Emillia Hawkins clock on with all the latest news and reader views for a Sunday featuring the Premier League fixture of the weekend. Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United at Anfield just days after wrapping up his reign as USA men’s coach. Victory would give him instant momentum as he fights to lift the club up the table. Earlier, hard-charging Brighton will fancy their chances against Hull, who have not won a Premier League match since August. For breaking news, reader input and good vibes aplenty – join the conversation at matchday.live@theguardian.com.

Emillia Hawkins and John Brewin keep track of Sunday’s WSL fixtures from midday as Birmingham face Manchester United and Charlton host Aston Villa. Then it is Everton v Brighton at 2pm followed by a London derby as Rita Guarino’s in-form West Ham visit Arsenal, with the Irons having notched four wins in their past five matches in all competitions. The Gunners are toiling, and they sit sixth in the standings going into the weekend, with just three wins from their opening 10 matches.

Second-placed Brighton have become the most unlikely title contenders with their free-scoring football and have every chance of continuing to defy the sceptics as they take on Hull. The Seagulls are the league’s top scorers with 26 goals, 11 more than Arsenal, and have the second-tightest defence, with just seven goals conceded.Join Dominic Booth for minute-by-minute coverage, with Aaron Bower reporting from MKM Stadium.

Rob Smyth buckles up for the big one at Anfield with all eyes on the latest United manager, Mauricio Pochettino. United’s tally of eight points and one win after 10 games is their lowest at this stage of a league season for 40 years. The former Southampton, Spurs and Chelsea manager says he needs time to turn the dysfunctional club’s fortunes around but he will be aware of the need to show progress quickly, with Liverpool in no mood to offer their most bitter rivals any favours. Looking for omens? The Argentinian’s first game for Chelsea was against Liverpool, which ended in a 1-1 draw at Stamford Bridge. Andy Hunter and Jamie Jackson make up our reporting team on Merseyside.

Daniel Harris offers live coverage of the final from Turin as the season-ending indoor hard-court tournament featuring the top eight singles players and top eight doubles teams draws to a thrilling close.

Graham Searles returns with his essential NFL liveblog covering the seven 6pm clashes. The division-leading Buffalo Bills (8-1), who boast the top scoring offence and second-best rush attack in the NFL, meet the Miami Dolphins (1-8) in the big AFC East clash. The other early Sunday games are Bears v Saints, Lions v Buccaneers, Panthers v Ravens, Cowboys v Titans, Chiefs v Cardinals, and Eagles v Steelers.

#803. 'I felt like I was a ghost' - when players miss a season through injury

Tottenham have played 50 Premier League games since Dejan Kulusevski's last top-flight start in May 2025

"I told my mother. I sat with her and I told her: 'Listen, I don't think I can play any more'," says Dejan Kulusevski in a moving interview about his injury nightmare.

It is 18 months since Tottenham and Sweden winger Kulusevski, 26, last started a competitive match.

Spurs have won the Europa League, sacked both Ange Postecoglou and Thomas Frank, "mutually agreed" to part ways with Igor Tudor and appointed Roberto de Zerbi since the former Juventus player last started a first-team game for his club.

A serious knee injury two weeks from the end of the 2024-25 season forced him to miss the whole of the following campaign, as well as the 2026 World Cup.

"You feel like the whole world has forgotten about you," adds Kulusevski in an interview with Tottenham's in-house media, external about the emotional toll of being out for so long.

Thankfully, the player nicknamed 'Deki' has made a full recovery and is closing in on his first Tottenham start since 11 May 2025.

He is not the only footballer to question their career after having their world turned upside down by injury.

In the women's game, Everton club captain Megan Finnigan recently returned from a cruciate ligament injury after 602 days out., external

"The amount of times the thought of retirement entered my head during rehab was a lot," Finnigan, 28, tells BBC Sport.

Countless hours in the gym away from team-mates, boredom, setbacks and frustration - what is it like for a player at the peak of their game to miss a season because of injury?

'I am a different man now' - Kulusevski on return after 526 days

Kulusevski out for a 'few months' - Postecoglou

Before Crystal Palace visited Tottenham a fortnight from the end of the 2024-25 campaign, Kulusevski had much to look forward to.

Off the pitch, he was making plans to marry his partner Eldina Ahmic, a former midfielder with Swedish club Brommapojkarna and Bosnia-Herzegovina.

On the pitch, there was a Europa League final against Manchester United coming up.

Everything changed in that match against Palace.

In the early stages, Kulusevski stayed down after a challenge with Marc Guehi. He was able to climb to his feet and walk unaided off the pitch and straight down the tunnel.

But in that moment, his problems were only just starting.

Start of a nightmare for Dejan Kulusevski who goes down injured in May 2025 - and does not play again until October 2026

"It was pain, but it didn't hurt that much," Kulusevski says, recalling the patella and cartilage injury in his right knee.

"I could feel that the knee was moving a little bit too much."

The initial diagnosis from Tottenham was that the Â£25m signing from Juventus, who arrived in the summer of 2023, would be out for "at least a few months".

Due to complications, those months turned into a year and Kulusevski's dream career threatened to turn into a nightmare.

He travelled to Bilbao on crutches to watch his team-mates beat United in the Europa League final.

"That was one of the hardest days of my life," he says. "It was so beautiful to see all the people happy, but for me I was going there with crutches, I couldn't work.

"I couldn't even go and get my medal because it was too slippy to go on that thing [platform].

"Seeing the team celebrating on the bus [outside Tottenham Hotspur Stadium] was probably one of the most difficult parts of this journey because you feel so alone.

"You feel like the whole world has forgot about you and what you put in."

As months went by, Kulusevski underwent multiple operations and was even offered a knee transplant as a treatment option, which he rejected.

"You get stressed because nothing works," he says.

Then came another crushing blow delivered in a phone call with Sweden boss Graham Potter. Stockholm-born Kulusevski, who had played for his country since the age of 19, would not be going to the 2026 World Cup.

He had hoped to recover in time to be selected.

"I just stared at the wall for three hours because I really believed I would do it," he says.

It is not just the players who suffer when they are out for so long; the people around them feel the emotional toll as well.

"Seeing him miss the Europa League final and the World Cup, every Premier League game last season, seeing him skipping around on his crutches, those parts were really difficult," Eldina, Kulusevski's wife, says.

'Fantastic moment, fantastic human' - De Zerbi on Kulusevski's long-awaited return

As recently as this past summer, Kulusevski wondered whether he would play again.

"It had been one year and two months and I could still not walk up the stairs like a normal guy.

"I wasn't going to give up, but I also had to think if this didn't work out, what am I going to do, because I am 26 and I have to have some sort of plan."

Enormous comfort came from Leonie, Kulusevski's two-year-old daughter, during his bleakest days.

"I said if I cannot play football any more, I will still have fun with her."

Then, after multiple setbacks, came a crucial breakthrough.

His knee had healed sufficiently for specialists to give him permission to train again.

On 19 October, Kulusevski was given a hero's reception by Spurs fans when he made his first appearance in 526 days.

It came in Tottenham's 3-1 win over Coventry City as an 87th-minute substitute.

Waiting for him after the final whistle were Eldina and Leonie, his daughter wearing a Spurs shirt with the number 526 on the back, along with the words 'My Hero'.

He made his Sweden return this month, coming off the bench in a win against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

"Every day is just beautiful now," says Kulusevski, who has made four substitute appearances totalling 42 minutes for his club this season.

Research suggests female footballers are two to six times more likely to suffer anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries than their male counterparts.

Everton captain Finnigan remembers how she "completely lost my sparkle" as she endured the long road to recovery.

"It's not comfortable to think back how I was," Finnigan tells BBC Radio Merseyside's Giulia Bould.

"Anyone that knows me knows I'm very bubbly, quite loud, I like to be at the centre of things. I completely lost myself in rehab, completely lost my sparkle as my mum says.

"How I was in this building is not nice to think back on. I was always thinking what other people were thinking about me. I was not pleasant to be around as I was struggling so much.

"I was also thinking 'no-one wants to be around me'. I was just miserable. Everyone in this building has seen me cry over the past 18 months."

Listen: Megan Finnigan 'Really special feeling to be back'

Megan Finnigan, Everton's number 20, returned to competitive action this season after 602 days out following an ACL injury

Finnigan - Everton's longest-serving women's player having joined the Blues at the age of nine - suffered her injury in an FA Cup tie against Tottenham in January 2025. She did not return to competitive action until September of this year.

"I was in quite a difficult place mentally," she adds.

One thing that helped her through her lowest moments was writing down her feelings.

"It was an absolute whirlwind of a rehab, a rollercoaster," she adds.

"Anyone who went through it with me will tell you that. I am really glad I kept a diary as proof I did it and survived it."

Former Arsenal and England midfielder Fara Williams points to how some players who suffer serious injuries in the Women's Super League face specific worries.

"While they are going through rehab, there are financial worries, bills to pay; they are on short contracts so you don't have that stability," says Williams.

"While you are managing the injury, mentally you are stressing, wondering where the next contract is coming from. When you are stressed, I imagine that doesn't help with the healing of the injury."

Micah Richards suffered multiple long-term knee and hamstring injuries before he retired in 2019 while at Aston Villa.

A few months later the former Manchester City and England defender opened up to BBC Sport about injuries and the "dark side of football".

"I was in a lonely place for a long time, and I did not know how to get out of it," he said at the time.

"Deep down, I probably knew it was already over, but for most of the two and a half years between my 295th and final game as a professional, against Wolves in October 2016, and the day I announced my retirement in July 2019, I was living in denial.

"I could run and I could jump - but I couldn't twist on my right knee, and it would not get any better. Whatever I tried, it did not make any difference.

"There were times while I was injured at Villa when I felt like I was a ghost.

"They told me to come in three times a week, then two. Then one.

"I would go into the gym and tell myself 'I am all right, I am all right, I am all right' but actually I had no idea how to deal with what was happening to me, and my body."

Tottenham fan Kish Patel explains how Dejan Kulusevski could fit into Roberto De Zerbi's starting XI
